We’re hiring a People Relations Business Partner to lead Duolingo’s approach to employee relations, leaves of absence, and workplace accommodations. You will serve as a trusted advisor to Duos, managers, and People Business Partners, bringing sound judgment and consistency to complex employee matters. You’ll manage employee relations cases, own our leave and accommodations programs, and use insights across this work to strengthen our practices and employee experience as Duolingo grows globally.

🧠 You will...

•
Employee Relations

• Manage Employee Relations Cases: Lead employee relations matters from intake through resolution, including employee concerns, workplace conflicts, conduct issues, and other sensitive situations.

• Conduct Investigations: Lead fair, thorough, and timely workplace investigations, documenting findings and partnering with Legal and People Business Partners on appropriate next steps.

• Advise Managers & PBPs: Provide practical guidance on employee concerns, performance and conduct matters, policy interpretation, and complex workplace situations.

• Build ER Practices: Develop tools, guidance, documentation standards, and case management practices that support consistent and thoughtful decision-making.

• Partner Across the Business: Work closely with People Business Partners, Legal, and other People teams to navigate complex or high-risk employee matters.

Leaves & Accommodations

• Own the Programs: Lead Duolingo’s global leave of absence and workplace accommodations programs, including program strategy, employee experience, policies, processes, and continuous improvement.

• Lead Accommodations: Manage workplace accommodation requests from intake through implementation and follow-up, partnering with Duos and managers to identify effective, reasonable solutions.

• Navigate Complex Leaves: Serve as the internal expert and escalation point for complex leave matters, partnering with external administrators, Benefits, Legal, managers, and People Business Partners.

• Support Return to Work: Guide complex return-to-work situations and transitions between leave and workplace accommodations.

• Manage Vendor Performance: Establish clear expectations for external leave and accommodations partners and hold them accountable for service, accuracy, timeliness, and employee experience.

• Support Our Global Workforce: Partner with regional People Business Partners and Legal to navigate leave and accommodation matters across geographies and local requirements.

Insights & Program Improvement

• Surface Trends: Analyze employee relations, leave, and accommodation activity to identify recurring themes, emerging risks, and opportunities for improvement.

• Look Beyond the Case: Connect patterns across individual cases to broader questions about management practices, workload, role design, policies, benefits, accessibility, and the employee experience.

• Turn Insight Into Action: Partner with People leadership, PBPs, Benefits, and Legal to translate what we’re learning into practical improvements.

• Measure Effectiveness: Develop meaningful measures of program health, including timeliness, consistency, outcomes, employee experience, and vendor performance.

People Team Support

• Support PBP Priorities: Provide coordination and project support across select People Business Partner priorities, including documentation, reporting, research, and process work.

• Drive Follow-Through: Help keep defined PBP workstreams organized and moving, bringing strong attention to detail, judgment, and execution.

✅ You have...

• 5+ years of experience across employee relations, workplace accommodations, leave management, HR, or related areas, including experience independently managing complex employee matters.

• Experience conducting workplace investigations and navigating sensitive employee relations matters from intake through resolution.

• Strong working knowledge of workplace accommodations and leave practices, including the ADA, FMLA, and interactive process.

• Experience advising managers and People partners on complex employee situations and translating policies and legal requirements into practical guidance.

• Strong judgment and the ability to navigate sensitive or ambiguous situations with consistency and discretion.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including clear, objective case documentation.

• Strong case management and organizational skills, with careful attention to confidentiality and follow-through.

• Ability to identify patterns across individual cases and translate them into broader organizational insights.

• Comfort working across teams, functions, and geographies in a fast-moving environment.

⭐ Exceptional candidates will have...

• Global Experience: Experience supporting employee relations, leaves, or accommodations across multiple countries or regions.

• Investigations Expertise: Significant experience independently conducting complex workplace investigations.

• Program Building: Experience building or scaling employee relations, leave, or accommodations practices.

• Vendor + System Management: Experience overseeing case management, external leave or accommodations administrators and using performance data to improve service.

• Systems & Insights: Experience using case management systems and employee data to identify trends and inform organizational decisions.

Watershed is the enterprise sustainability platform. Companies like Airbnb, Carlyle Group, FedEx, Visa, and Dr. Martens use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive real decarbonization. We are looking for team members who love product-building, want to work hard at a mission-oriented startup, and will collaborate with us in shaping the culture of a growing team.

We have offices in San Francisco, New York, Denver, London, Paris, Berlin, Sydney, Mexico City, and remote team members across the US and Europe. We hope that you'll be interested in joining us!

The role

We are looking for a customer-focused and analytically-minded person to join the Sustainability Data Advisory team in our San Francisco or New York office on a fixed-term basis, starting in December 2026. This is a chance to join a core team at a growth-stage startup that works with the world's top companies to speed up their sustainability programs. You'll work directly with customers as a trusted advisor, leading measurement sessions and delivering advisory services that unlock the full value of our platform. You'll help customers get clear, reliable insight into their sustainability impact and reach their sustainability goals.

You will:

• Advise sustainability teams at many of the world's top companies. You'll work directly with customers on how to measure actionable carbon and non-carbon footprints to reach sustainability goals and enable real reductions. The work ranges from scoping new measurements to in-depth methodology comparisons between footprints.

• Deliver services that speed up customer success. You'll help customers set up their measurements to meet sustainability goals, act as a trusted partner in emissions verifications, and give specialized advice to improve their data and methodologies. You'll make sure customers get the most out of Watershed's platform, faster and more effectively than they could on their own.

• Collaborate with science, engineering and product teams to build new measurement solutions and expand Watershed's sustainability intelligence layer.

You might be a fit if you:

• Have 2–4 years of experience in a consulting, solutions-engineering or other customer-facing role. You are excited to work directly with customers to help them set the foundation for world-class sustainability programs.

• Have experience in sustainability-related fields, greenhouse gas accounting and/or ESG reporting.

• Are an excellent verbal and written communicator. You can explain complex topics to technical and non-technical audiences.

• Learn quickly and work well in ambiguity. You are organized, systematic and efficient, and you thrive in a high-volume environment.

• Think clearly about complex problems and are comfortable using and speaking to data. You are meticulous and detail-obsessed.

• Are passionate about solving climate change and excited to help do so at a fast-paced startup.

Fixed-term details

• Minimum commitment of 4 months, with a possible extension of up to 3 more months.

• Fixed-term employees receive compensation and benefits similar to full-time Watershed employees, including daily lunch delivered in the Watershed office.

About the team

Trust & Safety keeps Patreon welcoming and fair, so creators and their fans can connect and creativity can thrive. We set clear standards and act quickly and consistently when something's off.

Porto is our main Trust & Safety hub in Europe, where a significant share of our safety work gets done. It's a close-knit, multidisciplinary team of content specialists, project and program managers, vendor managers and policy experts, sharing the office with colleagues in Support, Fraud and Compliance. As Patreon grows into a place where fans discover new creators and communities, the work done in Porto matters more than ever.

About the role

We're looking for an experienced operations leader to run Trust & Safety in European hours and lead our Porto site.

As T&S Operations Lead, you'll own how well Porto runs: healthy queues, targets met, smooth handoffs to our US team, and a team that knows what's expected and how they're doing. Operational excellence, team enablement, and capacity planning are at the heart of the job.

You'll be the senior operations leader on site from day one, with a direct report focused on operations enablement and a scope built to grow as Porto does, including leading more of the site's team over time. You'll work hand in hand with our global Trust & Safety leaders on policy, quality, tooling, and partner management, and bring Porto's perspective into the decisions that shape how we keep Patreon safe.

• Plan capacity. Work with the leaders of each safety area and our program managers to build monthly capacity plans across our in-house team, outsourcing partners and automation, and rebalance work when volume shifts.

• Deliver on our targets, and find out why we miss. The leaders of each safety area set targets for their work and agree them with you. You'll be the single place those goals come together for Porto: deliver them on the ground, track progress, coach the team, and dig into root causes when we miss on efficiency or quality, then bring back what you learn.

• Raise the bar on how we operate. Co-own the playbooks, training and workflow changes our safety-area leaders and program managers design, lead their rollout in Porto, and measure the impact on quality, handle time and backlog.

• Keep work moving between Europe and the US. Make sure escalations, incidents and open work hand off cleanly across time zones, so nothing stalls or drops.

• Lead incidents in European hours. Contain issues using our playbooks, make the call when a decision can't wait, and hand off with full context.

• Look after the team. Make sure people doing high-exposure work have the rotation, breaks and support they need, notice early signs of strain, and involve people before changes that affect them.

• Lead the site. Chair the Porto Leadership Council, bringing together every team in the Porto office, from Support to Fraud and Compliance. Be Porto's voice with US leadership, and build a culture where people feel connected and recognized.

What you'll own

• Your call, for Trust & Safety in Porto: running our operations day-to-day in European hours. That includes keeping work flowing when volume spikes, covering absences, containing incidents using our playbooks, and setting the team's operating rhythm. Other teams in the office keep their own leadership.

• Your call, for the Porto site: the Porto Leadership Council’s agenda and how Porto shows up with Execs and US leadership. Other non-T&S teams keep their own leadership. You align and represent them, you don’t manage them.

• Agreed with the leaders of our safety areas: the targets they set for their work, monthly capacity plans, shifting work between areas, and workflow changes that affect enforcement decisions.

• Owned by partners, with your input: policy and enforcement standards, quality standards, HR matters and vendor contracts. You'll have a strong voice in all of them.

About you

• 8+ years leading content moderation, Trust & Safety or customer support operations. Whether in-house or at an outsourcing partner, you've run the people, targets, and quality of a content or customer-facing team. Workforce management and quality leadership in those settings count too.

• You have a track record of moving the numbers. You've owned throughput, quality, and service-level goals for an operations team, built capacity plans, and delivered measurable improvements you personally drove.

• You've scaled operations with outsourcing partners or automation.

• You lead with clarity and fairness. You set expectations, give direct feedback with care, and stay calm when things get hard.

• You work well across teams. You've led alongside teams you don't manage, and you know when to decide and when to align.

• You're fluent in English. Portuguese is a strong plus.

• You're based in Porto, or ready to relocate. We'll support your move.

Nice to have

• Trust & safety experience, especially with EU/UK online-safety rules.

• Experience leading a site or office in Portugal or elsewhere in Europe.

• Experience with AI-assisted moderation or quality programs.

What success looks like in your first year

• Review rates and handoffs in European hours are consistently on target.

• T&S has a clear, reviewed capacity plan, updated monthly.

• Quality findings turn into action within 90 days.

• The Porto Leadership Council meets on a regular cadence with agreed site priorities.

• The Porto team feels more connected and more confident in where they're headed.

Why join

• Lead a site. Shape how our main Trust & Safety hub in Europe runs, with real decision rights from day one.

• Room to grow. A clear path to leading more of Porto's team as the site grows.

• Meaningful work. Help keep a community of millions of creators and fans safe.

• Life in Porto. One of Europe's most livable cities, on the Atlantic coast.

Along with your CV, answer one short question (a few sentences is plenty): tell us about an operation you led. How many people, what volume, and one metric you improved? If one of our recruiters reached out to you, we'll cover this in your first call instead.

Finance’s mission is to Accelerate, Advise, and Protect the business. Our FP&A team is organized around capital allocation, and we hold every major investment to three questions:

• Before: Is this the best use of capital?

• During: Is it performing as expected?

• After: Was this a good use of money?

You’ll own the numbers leadership and the board use to run Patreon: the plan, the forecast, and the story behind the company’s performance. You’ll also own company-wide headcount, our largest investment, and make sure every role we add is the right use of capital. We cross-train, so you’ll get to know the whole business, not just your part of it, and step in for teammates when needed.

We’re also past the “try AI” phase. Finance runs FinHacks, team-wide build days where we automate real workflows. Our first was about learning; our second is about shipping, from flux and financial model automation to executive headcount reporting and month-end close. You’ll bring that same approach to every part of your role.

Corporate Reporting

• Own the monthly and quarterly reporting cycle, from P&L variance and KPIs to the commentary and materials for leadership reviews, board meetings, and investor updates

• Maintain the core financial model and source-of-truth metrics, partnering with Accounting (NetSuite) and Data

• Streamline the planning and reporting processes, and automate the manual parts

Company Headcount

• Assumptions: Set, test, and refine the assumptions behind headcount cost, such as benefits and payroll taxes, attrition, merit and promotion increases, and hiring timing, so the forecast stays accurate

Cross-Functional Support

• Lean in on G&A and other business partnership work when the team needs it, from budget support to investment and spend reviews

• You’ve run a full planning cycle and built the forecast story that leadership and the board rely on

About the Role

The New York Times is rebuilding how we use people data. Instead of one-off reports and ad hoc pulls, we are building governed, reusable data tools that HR leaders, HR partners, and their counterparts use to make decisions. You will help build this layer. People data at The Times lives in several systems, each with its own definitions and history. You will turn that into a modeled, tested, documented foundation that products can be built on repeatedly. You will lead the models, transformations, and data quality behind every product this team ships. You will report to the Senior Director, People Data and Insights. You will work out of the New York office on a hybrid schedule.

Responsibilities:

• You will design, build, and maintain the data models and databases that our products run on.

• You will oversee the transformation layer from source systems into governed, tested, documented models.

• You will turn metric definitions from the data dictionary into executable logic, so that a definition and the number it produces cannot drift apart.

• You will build data quality into the pipeline: tests, validation, and reconciliation across sources that surface problems before team members do.

• You will work with the Program Manager to translate product requirements into models, and push back when a requirement and the underlying data do not agree.

• You will handle effective-dated and historical data correctly, so that point-in-time questions get point-in-time answers.

• You will implement and maintain access controls appropriate to compensation, demographic, and other sensitive data.

• You will document models and lineage so that all can understand why something was built the way it was.

• You will demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications

• 5+ years of experience in analytics engineering, data engineering, or an equivalent role building production data models.

• You are a SQL expert

• Strong dimensional modeling skills, and the judgment to know when to normalize and when not to.

• 5+ years of experience with a transformation framework such as dbt, and with version control and code review as part of normal practice.

• 5+ years of experience handling slowly changing dimensions, dated records, and point-in-time reporting.

Preferred Qualifications

• 2+ years of experience with HR or people data, and with systems such as Workday, Greenhouse, or One Model.

• Python for orchestration, API work, or data validation.

• 2+ years of experience with AWS data services.

• Familiarity with BI and analytics tooling such as Hex, Tableau, or Looker.

• 2+ years of experience in an organization with distinct populations operating under different rules, such as union and non-union groups.

Our Mission
At Big Health, our mission is to help millions back to good mental health by providing fully digital, non-drug options for the most common mental health conditions. Our FDA-cleared digital therapeutics—SleepioRx for insomnia and DaylightRx Treatment for anxiety—guide patients through first-line recommended, evidence-based cognitive and behavioral therapy anytime, anywhere. Our digital program, Spark Direct, helps to reduce the impact of persistent depressive symptoms.

In pursuit of our mission, we’ve pioneered the first at-scale digital therapeutic business model in partnership with some of the most prominent global healthcare organizations, including leading Fortune 500 healthcare companies and Scotland’s NHS. Through product innovation, robust clinical evaluation, and a commitment to equity at scale, we are designing the next generation of medicine and the future of mental health care.

Our Vision
Over the next 5-10 years, we believe digital therapeutics will transform the delivery of healthcare worldwide by providing access to safe and effective evidence-based treatments. Big Health is positioned to take the lead in this transformation.

Big Health is a remote-first company, and this role can be based anywhere in the US.
Position Summary
Prescription digital therapeutics are one of the newest categories in healthcare, and most practices have never ordered one. That's changing fast. Medicare has created billing codes for digital mental health treatment, providers want evidence-based, non-drug options for insomnia and anxiety, and our treatments are FDA-cleared. What most practices are missing is someone who can show them how it works and get them ordering.
That's this role. You'll own growth with smaller practices and practices that come to us through our referral model and referral partners. You'll take them from the first conversation to the first order, then build them into steady, repeat ordering. You'll also support our Sales Director and Territory Manager with selective outbound to priority accounts.
This is a sales role first. We're looking for someone who has carried a number selling into medical practices, likes the follow-through as much as the close, and wants to get in early on a category that's still being defined. You'll report directly to our Chief Revenue Officer (CRO), work closely with Sales, Provider Experience and Clinical Transformation (PECT), Key Accounts, and Market Access, and help write the playbook for how we grow this channel.

Why This Role
• Get in early on a new category. Digital treatment is becoming part of how care is delivered. You'll be one of the people who makes that happen in practices across the country.

• Sell something providers want. FDA-cleared, evidence-based, non-drug treatment for two of the most common conditions in primary care and behavioral health.

• Real visibility. You'll report to the CRO, and your results will show up directly in company growth.

• Build the channel. Our referral and practice channel is early. You'll shape the playbook and have room to grow as it scales.

Key Responsibilities
• Inbound and Conversion

• Own inbound interest from smaller practices and referral sources. Respond fast, qualify fit, and book next steps.

• Run discovery and demos with providers and practice managers: how SleepioRx and DaylightRx work, how ordering works, and how practices bill for digital treatment.

• Work your pipeline with consistent follow-up so interested practices don't stall between the first call and the first order.

• Route larger practices and health system opportunities to the Sales Director and Territory Manager based on agreed criteria.

• Onboarding and Activation

• Get new practices live using our onboarding playbook: account setup, ordering steps, patient communication, and activation.

• Train providers, MAs, and staff on ordering and on helping patients get started.

• Help practices work through billing questions with their own billing team, including digital mental health treatment codes (G-codes) and payer coverage. Bring in Market Access when it gets complicated.

• Drive every new practice to a first order, then to repeat orders from more than one provider.

• Account Management and Growth

• Manage a book of smaller and referral-partner practices once they're live, with scaled touchpoints: check-ins, office hours, webinars, and targeted outreach.

• Watch ordering and activation data, spot practices that are slipping, and act early.

• Grow ordering inside each practice by adding prescribers and expanding to new patient populations; identify opportunities for embedding the referral process into the practice workflow.

• Be the first line for practice questions and route technical, billing, or contract issues to the right internal team.

• Outbound

• This is a smaller, targeted part of the role.

• Run selective outreach to priority accounts and practice segments in support of the Sales Director and Territory Manager.

• Work our referral partner networks to generate new practice opportunities.

• Support conferences and events, including pre-event outreach, booth coverage, and post-event follow-up.

• Capture what works and what doesn't. Bring patterns back to the team to improve sales materials, onboarding, training, and care pathway templates.

• Keep Salesforce accurate and up to date, including activity, stage, pipeline, and next steps.

• Help test new ways to reach, convert, and support practices as we scale the referral model.

Our Mission and Opportunity

Early education is one of the most important determinants of childhood outcomes, a critical support for working families, and a $175B market that remains underserved by modern technology. Brightwheel is the largest, fastest growing, and most loved platform in early ed, trusted by millions of educators and families every day. We are a three-time Cloud 100 company , backed by top investors including Addition, Bessemer, Emerson Collective, Lowercase Capital, Notable Capital, and Mark Cuban.

Our Team

Our team is passionate, talented, and customer-focused. We embody our Leadership Principles in our work and culture. We are a distributed team with remote employees across every US time zone, as well as select offices in the US and internationally.

Who You Are

You are an AI-native product leader and builder who combines world-class product taste, deep customer empathy, and high standards with the drive to build something new, and you want that something to matter. You create clarity in ambiguous spaces, turn a first product line into a real business, and lead by example in how modern products get built. You care about the teacher who opens the app at 7:25 with nine toddlers arriving, the parent who wants to know their child is learning, and the state official who has to show what a year of funding bought. You move with the urgency and ownership of a founder.

You will succeed in this role if you are

• Here for the mission. You want the outcome measured in what children learn and what teachers can do, and you know that a business that grows is how that outcome reaches millions of children instead of thousands.

• Focused on customer and business impact. You care about creating real value for families and educators, and about proving a business that can grow into something meaningful for brightwheel.

• A practitioner-builder. You do not lead from a distance. You use AI and modern tooling in your own work to build, prototype, and learn, and to show what great looks like.

What You'll Do

The years before kindergarten shape everything that comes after, and early education is where the gap between children first opens. brightwheel sits at the center of it, trusted by tens of thousands of schools and millions of families, with the distribution and profitable core most founders never get to start with. Our education business is where that trust turns into outcomes: curriculum that gives a teacher a plan for the day, assessments that show a parent how their child is growing, and professional development that helps teachers get better at one of the hardest and least supported jobs in education. States and districts fund these years, set the standards, and need to see results against them. Entire companies exist to do just one of these pieces. None of them also runs the school.

About Brilliant

Brilliant is creating a world of better problem solvers. We deliver learning that's interactive, adaptive, and fun – at scale. You can learn more about our approach, learners, and method on our about page.

We have always prioritized building a real, healthy business, and we make hires very selectively and intentionally. We serve hundreds of thousands of paid subscribers, and want you to help us serve millions.

In our day-to-day, we value adventure, excellence, generosity, and candor. We are optimists in the face of uncertainty, we take pride in our work, we go the extra mile for each other, and we tell it like it is (the good and the bad). We’re here to do the best work of our lives together.

We believe that real-time collaboration and human connection are necessary ingredients in building a high-velocity, high-trust team. We maintain core hours (9:30am - 2:30pm Pacific) when everyone is online, regardless of timezone. About half of us are located near our hubs in SF and NYC.

In addition to what’s below, you can see all open roles and learn more about our culture on our careers page.

The Role

CS Learning Designers at Brilliant design interactive learning games to teach programming and algorithmic thinking. We’re hiring exceptional learning designers who can teach computer science concepts creatively using Python, as well as brainstorm new interactive experiences that bring the principles of algorithm design to life.

You will work in a small, nimble team to redefine the future of education. We especially encourage applicants with a strong background in computer science education to apply.

You will use your pedagogical instincts and taste to expand Brilliant’s library of CS learning games and achieve the best possible outcomes for our learners and our business. You will be joining a passionate and experienced team of entrepreneurial-minded people who are working to make a meaningful impact on the world.

To be considered for this role, please include your best example(s) of how you've taught computer science concepts interactively online.

Responsibilities
• Develop hands-on programming courses to teach CS concepts using Brilliant’s Python learning game.

• Design new learning games — visual, puzzle-driven experiences that teach foundational principles in algorithms, data structures, and computational thinking.

• Decompose complex computer science ideas (e.g., recursion, backtracking, dynamic programming) into approachable, well-sequenced steps that empower learners to reason from first principles.

• Design content that is clear, creative, and intuitive — using interactivity to help learners build confidence and mastery.

• Build immersive, interactive learning experiences that guide learners along problem-solving journeys.

• Collaborate with product, design, and engineering teams to imagine and create new interactive features, visuals, and mechanics that elevate the learning experience on both computers and phones.

You
• Have an undergraduate degree or above in a STEM field, and you’ve developed a strong grounding through research or teaching that extends beyond traditional curricula.

• You have used AI agents extensively for coding, and have an opinionated stance on what core concepts are important to teach in the world of agentic coding.

• Have a knack for teaching complex topics using a progression of clear, simple, hands-on steps.

• You have experience with building or using interactivity to motivate, engage, and challenge learners, including in asynchronous contexts.

• Have a way with words, especially when communicating challenging concepts, and your writing skills (in English) are top notch.

• Are great at context switching and prioritizing among a large workload.

• Have an openness to change and a willingness to experiment with formats and platforms.

• Are not afraid to jump into any aspect of a project to fill a vacuum, no matter how big or small.

Compensation and Benefits

We use a systematic compensation framework: salary scales are set each year for each job vertical, managers level folks on their team, and those levels are mapped directly to our compensation scales. A location-based adjustment is applied outside of SF and NYC (typically 5-10%) - feel free to ask us about your location!

Given the systematic approach, we always make First and Best offers - there is no negotiation (for new hires nor our existing teammates). This ensures people are paid based on their expected contribution, not their negotiation skills.

We offer top-notch health care plans, with 100% of the premiums covered for medical, dental, and vision for employees.

We offer flexible PTO, with a norm of taking off about 6 weeks per year (including federal holidays). We also provide home office equipment, a professional development stipend, and free food at our offices.

Every Celonis outcome starts with data. As a Solutions Architect, you make sure our customers’ data gets into the Celonis Platform reliably, securely, and at scale, and that insights and actions flow back out into the systems and AI tools where work actually happens.

You’ll join our customer programs team as one of the first technical faces of Celonis. You’ll work hands-on across the full integration toolkit: deploying our out-of-the-box extractors, building custom API connectors in a low-code environment, writing code for push-based ingestion, connecting Celonis to customer lakehouses and LLMs, and configuring writebacks, SSO, and user provisioning. Part implementation consultant, part integration engineer, part trusted technical advisor, this role is ideal for someone early in their career who wants broad exposure to enterprise architecture and modern data and AI integration patterns.

What You’ll Do

Data integration and ingestion

• Implement standard extractors. Install, configure, and troubleshoot Celonis out-of-the-box extractors in customer landscapes, including SAP (ECC and S/4HANA), JDBC-based databases, and cloud applications such as Salesforce, ServiceNow, and others.

• Build custom API connectors. Design and build custom connectors with Celonis Extractor Builder for source systems that expose data through REST or SOAP APIs, handling authentication (OAuth 2.0, API keys, certificates), pagination, rate limits, and incremental (delta) loads.

• Enable push-based ingestion. Help customers design and develop scripts and pipelines (typically in Python) that push data to Celonis via the Data Ingestion API, and advise on file formats, scheduling, and error handling.

• Connect to the lakehouse. Set up zero-copy data sharing between Celonis and customer lakehouses such as Databricks and Microsoft Fabric, including Delta Sharing configuration, access controls, and data freshness.

Actions, AI, and platform connectivity

• Close the loop with writebacks. Configure Action Flows and other integration patterns that write back to customer systems (for example, updating records in SAP, Salesforce, or ticketing tools) so Celonis insights turn into action.

• Connect Celonis to AI. Help customers connect Celonis to their LLMs and AI agents through MCP, covering authentication, permissions, and governance.

Identity, security, and governance

• Own authentication and provisioning. Configure SSO (SAML, OIDC) with identity providers such as Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, and Ping, and set up SCIM-based user and group provisioning.

• Be the security translator. Support customer security, privacy, and compliance reviews, explain the Celonis architecture and data flows, and advise on topics like data minimization, pseudonymization, and least-privilege access.

Customer and team impact

• Scope with confidence. Run technical discovery, document integration architectures and requirements, and estimate effort so projects start on solid footing.

• Be the voice of the field. Escalate product gaps and bugs with clear, reproducible detail, and share field feedback that shapes our integration roadmap.

• Build reusable assets. Contribute reusable connector templates, scripts, runbooks, and best-practice documentation that scale across customers and partners.

• 2–5 years of experience in a technical, customer-facing role such as solutions engineering, integration or implementation consulting, data engineering, or technical consulting.

• Solid programming skills in Python (or a similar language) and strong SQL skills.

• Working knowledge of data pipelines and ETL/ELT concepts, including incremental loads, scheduling, and handling large data volumes.

• Familiarity with identity and access management concepts such as SSO (SAML/OIDC) and SCIM provisioning.

You’ll own a meaningful slice of the product: the important-but-less-nebulous work that keeps a democracy-facing platform trustworthy and scalable. You’ll also own the internal tools that let our program managers run local campaigns at scale, and the testing and analysis that tells us whether what we shipped actually worked.

The ideal candidate is an AI-native product manager who likes clear problems and rigorous follow-through. At the same time, AI-driven economic and social disruption will demand faster, more effective government responses than our institutions are built to deliver. We are building a product to surface the public will on major issues by combining large-scale civic input with informed, representative dialogue, then activate that will at scale by mobilizing millions to shift the incentives that shape public policy. By using the same technologies that threaten democratic legitimacy, we aim to give citizens more voice than ever before, identify shared agreement across political differences, and enable collective intelligence at scale.

Change.org is a public benefit company and the world’s largest social change platform, with 100M users and more than 40,000 campaigns launched monthly. Key outcomes

• Own the product work that keeps a democracy-facing platform trustworthy: moderation systems and rubrics, privacy and policy obligations (such as GDPR), and the due diligence that comes with a product close to public officials and public decisions.

• Own the internal tools and admin layer for our operations team. Much of what they do to scale campaigns, like city research, decision-making, and building materials for local government partners, isn’t productized yet. You’ll partner with a dedicated engineer to change that, treating ops as a core customer.

• Be the key liaison to the program managers who run our deliberation cycles. Support and coordinate across campaigns from the product side, from platform setup and audience acquisition through in-cycle monitoring and post-cycle reporting, so we build a cohesive product with them in mind and carry their insights, and those of our decision-maker users, back into what we build.

• Own experimentation and analysis: design and run A/B tests, carry testing through after features launch so it doesn’t pile up, instrument cycles, build dashboards, and write up findings the team can act on. Where we rely on LLM-based or human evaluation rubrics, audit them and make sure the signal we trust actually deserves it.

• Manage external partners and vendors—paid acquisition partners, tooling vendors, contractors, and other external collaborators—so internal partners aren’t task-switching into vendor coordination.

• Connect the pieces across groups, particularly marcoms and program management, so campaigns, launches, and product changes stay coordinated. Take the “par-baked” first pass on analyses and synthesis so product, design, and engineering can move faster.

• Handle user inbound requests, monitoring and creating a system to respond and learn from these inputs

• Extend the product management and design functions where needed—running discovery, drafting briefs, herding cross-functional initiatives, and bringing things over the line in code with the help of our Claude-centered AI development process.

The most important core competencies for the role are:

• Product Execution & Rigor: You design and run repeatable processes that compound. You treat internal tools and operational workflows as a product surface—designing, instrumenting, and iterating on them the same way you would on a feature. You’re comfortable owning the unsexy middle, and you get satisfaction when something boring becomes automatic.

• AI Fluency: You use AI tools fluently to multiply your output—drafting, analyzing, coding, automating, evaluating. You can stand up an LLM-based eval, run a deep research pass, or wire up a small agentic workflow to replace a manual task. You understand the difference between what AI is good at and where a human still needs to sit in the loop.

• Analytical Instincts: You can move from a fuzzy question to a clean answer. You’re comfortable in spreadsheets, SQL, and product analytics tools, and you know how to combine quantitative signal with qualitative read to tee up decisions. You take eval design seriously—you ask whether a metric measures what it claims to measure, and you redesign it when it doesn’t. You write up findings crisply and you don’t bury the lede.

• Experience in regulated or high-trust domains (benefits, payroll, fintech, health, trust & safety, or civic and policy teams at tech companies) is a strong plus

• Strong analytics chops: fluent in quant and qual analysis, comfortable with experimentation (A/B tests, holdouts), and familiar with product analytics tools (Amplitude, Mixpanel, or equivalent). Direct experience designing or auditing evaluation frameworks is a strong plus.

• Hands-on experience using AI tools to do real work—e.g., shipping prompts into a product, building LLM-based evals, using Claude Code or Cursor, or wiring together agentic workflows. Curiosity is not enough; we want to see what you’ve actually built or run.

About Dojo

Dojo started as a simple way for teachers to show parents what happened in class. Today it's used in 95% of US K-8 schools and by 1 in 4 American families, and reaches about 50 million kids in 180 countries. We got here with around 220 people and have never paid for a user.

Families trust us with their kids, and we're now building on that trust. On Dojo Islands, kids explore a shared world with their friends after school. Dojo Tutor connects families with tutors. Sparks is an AI tutor for every kid, and Login with Dojo will let children sign in safely anywhere online.

Our mission is to give every child on Earth an education they love. We hire for talent density, and many of our people came from Instagram, Netflix, Dropbox, Stripe, Uber and Y Combinator.

The job

Every product above lives in a category whose rules haven't been written yet. State legislatures, the FTC and the EU are writing them right now. What should a shared online world for eight-year-olds allow? How should an AI talk to a child? Who verifies a kid's identity, and what happens to that data? Some company will answer these questions well, in public, and earn the trust of parents and schools for a generation. We want that company to be Dojo, and we want you to lead it.

As Head of Legal you'll sit on the leadership team and work directly with our co-founders. You'll own all of legal: product, privacy, commercial, corporate, employment, IP, regulatory and litigation. You'll inherit good foundations, including a small in-house team, trusted outside counsel and working commercial and privacy processes. Your job is to make them great.

We have strong views on how this should work. Trust is our moat, and the right Head of Legal makes it deeper every quarter while teams ship faster. The best legal answer is usually a version of yes with sensible guardrails, reached early, before anyone has spent months building the wrong thing. We also think AI now lets a small team of exceptional lawyers do what used to take fifteen. You'll get to prove it.

Your first 18 months

Make Dojo the company parents trust most with their kids.

• Decide where Dojo stands on the hardest questions in kids' tech, and say it publicly before regulators decide for us: AI that talks to children, kids playing together online, and how products for kids should make money.

• Figure out which seals and certifications actually change a parent's or a district's mind, then win them.

• Make privacy one of the reasons districts pick Dojo.

• When a regulator calls, handle it so well that the product and our reputation come out unharmed.

Make legal the reason things ship faster.

• Get pulled into the room early by product, engineering and partnerships, because you make their plans better. Find the version that can ship, name the one or two real showstoppers, and tell the team what to do this week.

• Turn standard contracts in hours and product questions in two days.

• Write the playbooks that let district data agreements, partnerships and vendor deals close without starting from zero each time.

Build a legal team that outperforms teams five times its size.

• Lead and grow a small, very good in-house team, and hold outside counsel to budget and to your standard.

• Put AI into the daily work on contracts, data agreements and privacy reviews. Decide what comes in-house and what stays with specialists, so outside spend falls while quality rises.

• Own M&A, financing and board matters with our CFO, and keep the company ready to do a deal or a raise on short notice.

You will be a match if:

• You've led legal at a consumer tech company of 100 to 1,000 people, where product and engineering create most of the value.

• Product and business leaders who've worked with you say, unprompted, that you made them faster and found answers they hadn't seen. You end your advice with what you'd do, and once the call is made you own it.

• You've owned privacy for a consumer product, ideally one for kids, across COPPA, FERPA, state student privacy laws, CCPA/CPRA, GDPR and the new rules on AI. If your depth is narrower, you learn fast and already think about it clearly.

• You're comfortable running M&A, financings and board work alongside a CFO.

• You've led talent-dense teams and managed several outside firms to budget. You know the right specialist for almost any problem and can get them on the phone today.

• You've rebuilt legal work with AI yourself, and can explain concretely how three lawyers plus specialists can match fifteen.

• You turn a messy problem into the two or three decisions that matter, and you write short. You hold a position without starting a war, and you change your mind when the facts change, and you move decisions on trust rather than title.

• You move fast enough to make people slightly nervous, and you raise the bar on ambition as much as on rigor.

Bonus:

• 10+ years in law, ideally including child-directed products or student data.

• Time spent in strategy consulting, operating, finance or engineering.

• You've stepped into an existing legal function and made it markedly better, or led a distributed team.

• You can tell Dojo's story to a regulator, a reporter or a partner and leave them on our side.

You won't match every line here. If these problems make you want to start tomorrow, apply anyway. Some of our best people took unusual paths to get here.

Why now

Very few legal jobs let you shape how a generation of kids experiences the internet. The questions are new, the stakes are real, and the answers you reach here will set norms far beyond Dojo. You'll have the scale to matter, a team small enough that your judgment shows up in everything, and founders who want a real partner on the hardest calls.

• Build and maintain Excel models and workbooks to map data from ACE to client specific business rules.

• Design, build, and maintain automated workflows and data pipelines using N8N, Parabola, or equivalent tools to streamline audit analysis and reporting.

• Identify discrepancies, quantify duty and fee impact, and document audit findings with supporting evidence.

• Prepare clear audit reports and client-ready summaries of findings, root causes, and recommended corrective actions.

• Support remediation efforts resulting from audit findings, such as post summary corrections, prior disclosures, and refund or recovery filings.

An overview of this role

As the Corporate Development Director, you'll help influence how GitLab invests to win: what we build, what we buy, where we partner, and what we should not pursue. This role sits within the Corporate Development & Strategic Partnerships team, reporting to the VP, Corporate Development & Strategic Partnerships.

This role straddles strategy and M&A engagements. You'll lead research that frames GitLab's options: mapping the markets in and around our AI-powered DevSecOps platform, testing where we have a right to win, and turning that into clear recommendations for the executive team. When the answer is to acquire, you'll drive the deal process end to end, from outreach through close and integration.

Success here is not measured by deal count. It looks like sharper strategic choices: a well-reasoned point of view on our priority markets, investment theses that product and executive leaders rely on, acquisitions that speed up the roadmap when buying is the right answer, and an educated no when it isn't. You'll own the wider market perspective rather than individual product categories, and work with the team's Analyst on the research behind it.

What you'll do

Strategy and research

• Own the wider market view. Research the broader market GitLab competes in, beyond specific product categories: competitive dynamics, AI-native entrants, technology shifts and where value is moving. Collaborate with the team's Analyst on the research and turn the findings into a clear point of view on where GitLab should play.

• Build an investment thesis for each focus area. Work with Product and Engineering leaders to define the problems worth solving, the capabilities GitLab needs, and what it would cost in time and money to get there on our own.

• Own the competitive and landscape view. Maintain market maps and a current read on GitLab's competitors: their strategy, product direction, positioning, pricing, and M&A and funding activity. Produce competitor analyses that show where we lead, where we're exposed and how rivals are likely to move. Flag shifts by competitors, hyperscalers and AI labs that change our options, and bring the implications to Product and the executive team.

• Define where GitLab should not play. Identify adjacencies that dilute focus and markets where the economics or competition work against us. Make the case for a no with the same rigor as a yes.

Build, buy or partner

• Run the build, buy, partner analysis. For each strategic gap, compare the options side by side on speed, cost, risk, control and strategic fit, and bring a clear recommendation.

• Deliver strategic clarity to executives and the Board. Produce short strategy memos/decks and business cases that set out the decision, the trade-offs and what we give up with each path.

• Feed company strategy and planning. Bring an outside-in view of the market and the inorganic options available into annual and long-range planning.

• Work hand in hand with Strategic Partnerships. When partnering is the right answer, frame the opportunity and hand it to the partnership owner with a clear thesis. When it isn't, explain why.

Deal execution and integration

• Own end-to-end deal process management. Validate target fit against GitLab's our target profile, product roadmap and other criteria, and build the acquisition rationale and business case. Drive our M&A process from intro call through the various steps through to closing and integration.

• Evaluate the deal. Develop valuation, commercial integrity assessment, impact on GitLab's business and provide negotiations assistance to the VP and the executive team.

• Lead cross-functional diligence. Run pre-LOI validation and diligence across Product, Engineering, Security, Finance, Legal and People, and communicate findings clearly.

• Drive deal documents with Legal. Prepare NDAs, LOIs and purchase agreements with GitLab Legal and outside counsel.

• Own integration outcomes. Lead post-acquisition integration as the DRI, measured against the roadmap and business goals in the business case. Bring lessons learned back into the strategy work.

• Build the external network. Maintain relationships with founders, executives, investors, bankers and advisors that bring us early insight and pipeline.

What you'll bring

• Strategy and deal experience. 8+ years across corporate development, corporate strategy, strategy consulting or technology investing, including 5+ years leading acquisitions end to end in enterprise software.

• Structured strategic thinking. You form a point of view from incomplete information, test it against data, and change your mind when the evidence says so. You're as comfortable recommending that we stay out of a market as that we enter it.

• Market research depth. Skilled in market sizing, competitive analysis and landscape mapping, and in turning research into a recommendation, not a report.

• Deal craft. Skilled in valuation, financial modeling, deal structuring, negotiation and integration planning, with experience across varied consideration structures.

• Technical fluency. A working understanding of software development, DevSecOps and the AI landscape, enough to hold substantive conversations with product and engineering leaders about roadmaps and architecture.

• Clear executive communication. You write short, decision-ready updates and present trade-offs plainly to executives and the Board, in an async-first environment.

• Influence without authority. You build trust across Product, Engineering, Finance and Legal and move decisions forward across functions.

• Ownership with collaboration. You own the strategic view and the recommendation, and partner closely with the team's Analyst on research and analysis.

• Preferred: familiarity with the DevSecOps, security, AI and open source ecosystems.

• You value the all remote lifestyle and share our values .

About the team

The Corporate Development & Strategic Partnerships team helps GitLab decide how to grow beyond what we build on our own. We own inorganic strategy: acquisitions, strategic partnerships with hyperscalers and AI labs, and the research that tells us which to pursue and which to pass on.

We work across Product, Engineering, Finance, Legal and the executive group. We set direction and do the detailed work ourselves, with a high degree of ownership and transparency in a fully remote, asynchronous environment.

About the role

Join us to build the decision engine for better mental health outcomes.

As a Senior Data Scientist, you will sit in the heart of a cross-functional product team and help turn messy, real-world signals into clear decisions. You will make sure we are capturing the right data, designing experiments that tell us what is actually driving outcomes, and translating findings into recommendations that teams can act on quickly. When the insight is stable and valuable, you will help operationalize it through predictive models that improve provider and patient experiences.

We’re looking for people who like ambiguity, enjoy hard problems, and want their work to matter in the world.

What you will do

• Be the analytics partner inside the pod. Work closely with Product, Engineering, Design, Ops, and Clinical stakeholders to define the questions, the metrics, the guardrails, and the decision rules.

• Design and analyze A/B tests and quasi-experiments with clear hypotheses, power considerations, and pre-defined success criteria.

• Connect behavior to strategy. Use funnel, cohort, segmentation, and lifecycle analysis to understand how people and providers experience Headway, and where product changes will have the biggest impact.

• Use causal inference when experiments are not possible. Apply approaches like diff-in-diff, matching, and regression-based designs with principled uncertainty quantification.

• Develop predictive models that operationalize vetted insights (feature development, validation, backtesting, calibration), with clear launch criteria and monitoring plans.

• Produce analysis and narratives that are crisp, honest about uncertainty, and drive action.

• Help raise the bar by contributing to shared standards for metrics, experimentation, and analytical quality, so teams can move faster with confidence.

What will make you successful

• 6+ years using data to drive product or business decisions in product, growth, health, engineering, or operations environments.

• Strong SQL and strong proficiency in Python or R for analysis and modeling.

• Depth in experimentation and causal inference under real-world constraints.

• Fluency with AI tools as part of your workflow: using LLMs and coding assistants to accelerate analysis, prototyping, and documentation, while still owning the judgment and rigor behind the output.

• Practical modeling skill: feature engineering, model comparison, cross-validation or backtesting, calibration, and post-launch monitoring.

• Strong product sense and opinions, including a track record of connecting analytics recommendations to measurable outcomes.

• Clear communication: you can explain complex work to non-technical audiences without losing the truth.

• A self-starter mindset: you prioritize well, follow through, and do not need heavy oversight.

• Motivation for our mission: improving access and affordability in mental healthcare.

Where you could land

Data Science at Headway is structured around three core pillars, each focused on a distinct area of the business. Within each pillar, smaller pods own specific problem spaces, and several of those pods are actively hiring. We keep our interview process consistent across teams, and ahead of your preliminary call we’ll share a pre-read with details on the specific pods that are hiring so we can talk through where you might fit best.

• Patient: The Patient group owns how someone finds mental health care on Headway and gets to a provider who fits them: the first visit or phone call, search and matching, booking, and then attending a first appointment and staying in care. Data Science here means consumer funnel analytics, experimentation, and marketing science. That includes defining the metrics the group steers by, designing and reading experiments, and building causal and attribution methods for channels where you can't cleanly randomize. The modeling work spans ranking, matching, propensity, and the lifetime value and attribution models behind how we spend to acquire patients.

• Payer & Outcomes: The Payer & Outcomes group is responsible for driving best-in-class patient outcomes, building a trustworthy and safe provider network, and delivering value-based care with responsible costs relative to outcomes, both through product work across the company and by working directly with payers. On the Data Science side, there's room to go deep on product data science, commercial data science, or a mix of both: experimentation, causal modeling, forecasting, and sizing work. People are often drawn to this team by its rapid growth and by how directly the day-to-day work ties back to Headway's mission.

• Provider: Providers have real choices about where they build their practice. A provider might join Headway for credentialing, stay for reliable payments and tools that make the day easier, find new clients or bring over existing ones, or grow into a group practice. The Provider group owns that relationship and the trust it depends on, because we believe a clinician who feels supported can better help their patients. Data Science here is about understanding those choices: what draws a provider in, what keeps them, and what helps them grow with us. Experiments usually run at the provider level and often pair a product change with a conversation. Causal inference fills the gaps where randomization isn't possible. The models cover lifetime value, attribution, churn, and how providers respond to rates and incentives, along with work on how our tools support providers and their patients. Because the work spans product and go-to-market, Data Scientists here see the full provider relationship.

About the Web Platform team at Headway

Web Platform owns how Headway builds our frontend applications, including the UX. Web Platform sits in our Engineering Foundations organization, alongside our infrastructure and reliability team and our agentic engineering team. Every engineer who builds for the web at Headway builds on top of our work. When the platform is strong, product teams move faster and ship with higher quality. As the platform evolves to incorporate agentic engineering workflows, the team is positioned to become an even greater multiplier: using agents to build front-end code directly in line with Headway's standards, reducing the time and cognitive load product teams spend on front-end concerns so they can focus on business logic and product outcomes.

The team works across three areas:

• Design system: Helix is the shared language between Design and Engineering. Its components, tokens, and patterns keep what we design and what we ship the same across every Headway web app.

• Web architecture: We give engineers one clear way to build a Headway web app. This covers frameworks, build tooling, data loading, testing, performance, and accessibility across our patient, provider, internal, and marketing apps.

• Agentic UI: Headway engineers build with AI agents every day. We want those agents to build UI to Headway's standards by default. That takes a design system, patterns, and docs that agents can read, plus automated checks (visual regression, accessibility, and design system conformance) so that agent-written UI ships with confidence.

Principles that guide us:

• Focus on the mission: We view software as a means of effecting change in the world, not as an end unto itself. We write software to empower our patients and therapists to better solve the problems they're facing.

• Ship small, learn fast: We are building new and novel products and believe that we learn what our users need by quickly shipping and iteration.

• Everything is a product: Whether it's our patient search experience or a developer productivity improvement, we treat everything we build at Headway as a product with end-users in mind.

• Optimize for trust: We believe that engineers should be continually learning. To learn effectively and to be productive, engineers must feel safe asking questions and discussing mistakes.

Tools we use:

• Languages: TypeScript

• Libraries & Frameworks: React, React Router 7, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and Helix (our design system)

• Monitoring: Datadog, PagerDuty, Sentry

• Version Control: GitHub

• AI Tools: Cursor, Claude, Gemini, Eddy (our in-house cloud agent harness)

About this role

As the Senior Engineering Manager for Web Platform, you'll lead a small, senior team of five frontend engineers and own the vision for how Headway builds UI. This is the only role of its kind at Headway. You'll set the strategy for our design system and our web architecture, and you'll be the voice of frontend engineering across the company. The team doesn't have a dedicated product manager, so you'll set the roadmap with Design leadership and Engineering Foundations leadership, and you'll show the value of the work with clear metrics.

You'll stay close to the code. We expect you to be comfortable opening PRs, reading and changing code with AI tools, and taking on small pieces of work yourself, especially in your first few months. Larger projects stay with the team.

What you'll own

• Your team: Hire to a high bar, grow each person on purpose, and address underperformance directly. Give senior engineers ownership of technical direction, and make sure the team works as one team across all of its areas.

• Vision and strategy: Hold a clear, opinionated view of where Headway's frontend is going, and explain it to engineers, designers, and executives. Connect it to the Engineering Foundations strategy and to product roadmaps, and change it when the evidence says to.

• Design system and Design partnership: Evolve Helix with Design leadership as shared owners. Make the path from a design to production code short, so that designers and engineers start from the design system.

• Web architecture and standards: Own the frameworks and tooling that every Headway web app depends on, and the standards for accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA), performance, testing, and maintainability.

• Agentic UI: Give agents the skills, docs, and guardrails they need to write good frontend code. Build the automated checks and agent reviews that let that code ship with confidence.

• Frontend community: Grow our frontend guild at Headway. Learn from product engineers what's broken, and turn it into the roadmap.

• Priorities and headcount: Decide among planned work, support requests, and new bets, and keep the team from becoming a help desk. Make the case for the team size that Headway's frontend needs.

Who you are

• You've built your career in frontend. You were a senior or staff frontend engineer before you moved into management, and you have deep experience with React and the modern web.

• You've led a frontend platform, design system, or web architecture team, ideally at a fast-growing company.

• You've managed engineers for [3+] years. You've hired, grown senior engineers, and managed performance, including turning around or moving out someone below the bar. You don't need experience managing managers.

Eddy is Headway's in-house AI agent platform and the highest-leverage internal product we've shipped. It gives every Headwegian an agent harness pointed at Headway's own systems: an isolated sandbox per conversation, tool access to the third parties we depend on, and the ability to turn any of it into something durable, like a shareable interactive app, a workflow, a scheduled agent, a Slack teammate, or a webhook-triggered automation. Today 850+ Headwegians use Eddy daily, and 40k+ scheduled agents and workflows run every week with no one in the loop.

We sit in Engineering Foundations and own all of it: the chat product, the agent loop, the sandboxed runtime, the tool and integration layer, the artifact and app platform, the workflow engine, the eval harness, and the safety and access-control model that lets this touch real production and healthcare data without causing incidents. We're a small team with a very large surface area.

About this role:

Self-serve gets a function most of the way. It doesn't get them all the way.

Legal still reads every provider contract and payer amendment by hand, because what would help isn't a chat window. It's a system that knows what a redline means here, what gets escalated, and what our position was the last four times. Credentialing, claims exceptions, and CX triage each have their own version: work that is obviously automatable but full of enough domain-specific detail that nobody outside the function can build it, and nobody inside can build it alone.

That's this role. You'll embed with one function at a time and build them a real product on top of Eddy. Then you'll do the harder half: work out which parts are specific to that function and which are primitives that belong in the platform, and land the primitives in Eddy so the next function gets them for free. Most quarters should end with a function measurably better off and a new capability in the platform.

What you'll do:

- Find the real bottleneck. Sit with a function long enough to see the work, and define success in their terms: turnaround time, escalation volume, error rate, headcount avoided.

- Build the vertical. Skills, MCP integrations against their systems of record, subagents, scheduled and event-driven agents, artifact apps, and whatever product surface the workflow needs. You own it end to end.

- Ship in days, harden over weeks. Get a rough v1 in front of real users fast, then do the unglamorous work of making it dependable.

- Own it in production. Evals, tracing, cost and latency, failure modes. If a function depends on it, you're on the hook for it.

- Extract the primitives. Land the generalizable half in Eddy as a first-class capability, with tests and docs.

- Kill work that shouldn't exist. Some requests are better answered by a workaround, a config change, a process change, or nothing. Finding those is worth as much as building.

- Design for PHI from the start. Eddy operates inside HIPAA.

This is not solutions or sales engineering. There's no deal cycle, and your users are colleagues. It's not a pure platform role either: you'll spend real time inside other teams' problems.

AI: Claude Agent SDK, Anthropic API, Bedrock, LangSmith

Infrastructure: AWS, EKS (a hardened pod per session), EC2 + CodeDeploy blue/green, Temporal, Kafka, Cloudflare

Ops: Datadog, Sentry, PagerDuty, GitHub Actions

AI tools: Cursor, Claude Code, and Eddy itself. We build Eddy with Eddy.

- An end-to-end product builder who moves between a React surface, a FastAPI service, and a container image without a handoff.

- Serious about AI as engineering: tool use, agent loops, evals, context management, and cost and latency at volume.

About the Role:

The best SDETs in the industry are no longer measured by how many tests they write. They're measured by the systems they build that decide whether software is safe to ship — and, increasingly, by how well they wield AI to do it.

That's the role we're hiring for. We're looking for a Senior Staff SDET to own quality architecture and engineering strategy for our most critical systems, and to lead how we apply AI across our entire testing and release pipeline. You'll build the frameworks, platforms, and agent-driven workflows that the rest of engineering depends on, define what "safe to ship" means here, and stay deep in the code while doing it.

This is a genuinely hands-on senior technical leadership role with impact that spans many teams. If you want to build AI-native quality systems rather than bolt AI tools onto a legacy suite, this is that job.

Why This Role Is Different

• AI is the core of the work. You'll own how we use LLMs and agents for test generation, failure triage, self-healing, and release decisioning — and you'll set the guardrails that keep it trustworthy.

• You'll test AI, not just test with it. We ship AI-powered product features, which means building evaluation harnesses, golden datasets, and probabilistic assertions for systems that don't return the same answer twice. This is frontier work with very little established playbook.

• Real autonomy and real scope. You'll set the technical direction for quality engineering, not inherit someone else's strategy.

You Will:

Own quality architecture and strategy

• Own quality architecture for our most critical systems and initiatives, defining long-term quality strategy aligned with business and product goals.

• Design shared quality platforms, automation frameworks, and test infrastructure that are adopted across multiple teams.

• Establish quality patterns and guardrails that scale across teams, eliminating duplicated, brittle, or low-signal testing approaches through platform-level solutions.

• Anticipate systemic quality and reliability risks and drive preventative architectural solutions before they impact customers.

• Set the standard for what "great" looks like in quality engineering at scale.

Lead our AI-driven testing strategy

• Define and drive our strategy for AI-assisted testing — autonomous test generation, intelligent test selection, agent-based failure triage, and self-healing automation — with a clear-eyed view of where each genuinely pays off and where it adds noise.

• Build the guardrails that make AI-driven testing trustworthy: knowing when a self-healing agent is masking a real regression versus absorbing harmless implementation drift is the difference between leverage and liability.

• Orchestrate AI agents as part of the CI/CD decision pipeline, turning raw test signal into release confidence rather than more dashboards.

• Own quality for our AI-powered product features — designing eval suites, golden datasets, LLM-as-judge scorers, and statistical approaches for non-deterministic behavior, plus testing for hallucination, safety, and response stability.

• Establish how we test AI-generated application code, validating behavioral correctness and not just syntactic plausibility.

• Evaluate emerging AI testing tooling with real rigor, and be honest about what doesn't work.

Raise the bar operationally and across the team

• Lead the operational maturity of our quality systems and signals — defining quality metrics, dashboards, and release confidence indicators, and leading post-incident analysis that informs architectural and process improvements.

• Produce exemplary technical artifacts — quality architecture documents, automation frameworks, test platforms — that set the bar for the rest of the team, while staying hands-on in critical quality systems and automation code paths.

• Serve as the accountable technical leader for strategic initiatives, proactively managing reliability, scalability, and technical debt across teams.

• Mentor senior SDETs, quality engineers, and other senior technical leaders — especially on building AI fluency into their practice.

• Establish hiring standards, coaching, and talent development.

About the Role:

We are seeking a highly motivated, detail-oriented Manager, Production Planning to lead the planning team responsible for our non-sterile compounded production. This position manages and develops the site's production planners and owns the forward-looking production plan. The plan converts demand forecasts and inventory policy into a rolling view of the next several weeks through the next year or more, tests that plan against labor, equipment, and material capacity, and identifies where the business cannot meet it. The Manager then drives the response to each gap, whether through training, labor, or capital investment, and hands the plan to Production Scheduling for on-site execution. The ideal candidate is a proactive people leader with a strong understanding of integrated planning systems, supply chain dynamics, and cross-functional collaboration across the operations planning team.

You Will:

• Lead, manage, and develop the team of production planners, setting priorities, coaching, reviewing output, and ensuring consistent planning practices and coverage.

• Own the development and maintenance of mid- and long-term production plans for non-sterile compounded products in alignment with demand forecasts and inventory policies.

• Define the planning horizons, plan-of-record cadence, and frozen window, and publish the plan to Production Scheduling on a fixed schedule.

• Manage finished goods inventory for compounded products within company guidance while maintaining click-to-deliver metrics for customers.

• Develop what-if scenarios that identify where and when the plan exceeds available capacity, and which constraints are most sensitive to demand, product mix, batch size, and shift patterns.

• Articulate and document all risks resulting from production capacity constraints, including volume at risk, timing, and effect on delivery and inventory. If the plan cannot be met, make or recommend revisions when plans cannot be met, and document the reason for each revision.

• Recommend and size actions to close each gap, including training and cross-training for skill coverage, hiring and labor planning, overtime and shift design, equipment and facility investment, and outsourcing. Partner with Compounding Operations, HR, and Quality to carry out approved actions and track whether each one delivers the capacity it was sized to deliver.

• Monitor plan attainment, forecast accuracy, and capacity utilization at the weekly and monthly level, analyze variances, and implement corrective actions.

• Use actual cycle times, yields, and throughput reported by Production Scheduling to update planning standards and capacity model assumptions.

• Collaborate cross-functionally across the operations planning team, partnering with demand planning to communicate forecast discrepancies and agree on the plan of record, with production scheduling to confirm the plan can be executed and take in the constraints it escalates, and with procurement and raw materials planning to confirm material availability.

• Develop and maintain tools, dashboards, and KPIs that communicate plan status, constraints, risks, and performance to plan to leadership.

You Have:

• 8+ years experience in at least 1 of the following: Production planning, capacity planning, or resource planning, with demonstrated experience leading or developing others.

• Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Operations, Industrial Engineering, or related field required; APICS/CPIM certification a plus.

• Experience building capacity models and presenting investment, staffing, or outsourcing recommendations to senior leaders.

• Proficient in inventory management concepts with an understanding of the financial and operational implications of planning decisions.

• Experience in pharmaceutical or pharmacy production/manufacturing environments is a plus.

• Excel proficiency including experience with data manipulations – Lookups, PivotTables, External Data Connections.

• Basic SQL and/or Python experience is a plus.

• Deep knowledge of supply chain and manufacturing planning processes.

• Strong analytical skills and comfort with data-driven decision making.

• Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities and lead a team in a fast-paced environment.

As a therapist within our Pediatric Outpatient Service Line, you'll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact in the lives of children, teens, young adults, and their families while working as part of an integrated clinical team.
You'll provide evidence-based, developmentally appropriate therapy that helps members build resilience, strengthen relationships, develop effective coping skills, and make progress toward individualized treatment goals. Depending on the member's age and clinical needs, treatment may also involve partnering with parents or caregivers to reinforce skills, support treatment goals, and promote meaningful change outside of therapy sessions.
Therapists are an integral part of our collaborative care model. You'll work closely with behavioral case managers, psychiatric providers, nurses, coaches, and other clinical team members to ensure members receive coordinated care that reflects their individual, developmental, and family needs.
This role is a great fit for an independently NY licensed behavioral health clinician who is passionate about supporting children, teens, and young adults, values collaboration, and is comfortable adapting treatment across developmental stages. You'll have opportunities to expand your clinical expertise through consultation, ongoing training, evidence-based care practices, and collaboration with an interdisciplinary team.
