•
Provide evidence-based individual and family therapy to children, adolescents, young adults, and caregivers.

•
Conduct comprehensive behavioral health assessments and develop individualized treatment plans.

•
Utilize evidence-based modalities, including CBT, DBT, ACT, MI, PMT, trauma-informed interventions, and other approaches appropriate to the member's clinical and developmental needs.

•
Collaborate with psychiatrists, behavioral case managers, coaches, nurses, and other interdisciplinary team members to provide coordinated care.

•
Engage caregivers as active partners in treatment when clinically and developmentally appropriate through psychoeducation, collaborative goal setting, and skills coaching.

•
Maintain timely, accurate, clinically meaningful, and compliant documentation.

•
Participate in clinical consultation, supervision, ongoing training, and professional development.

•
Support quality improvement initiatives and the continued delivery of high-quality, evidence-based care.

Requirements:

Ability to work part-time, 24 hours per week.

•
Availability to provide care during afternoon and evening hours to support member scheduling needs.

•
Potential opportunity to work Saturdays based on program needs.

•
Ability to maintain a private, professional workspace appropriate for providing confidential telehealth services.

•
Ability to maintain reliable internet connectivity necessary to provide consistent, high-quality virtual care.

•
Must reside in and be authorized to work in the United States

•
Ability to meet applicable state licensing, credentialing, payer enrollment requirements, and interstate practice requirements.

Qualifications:

Current, active New York license and registration in good standing that permits independent clinical practice and diagnosis( LCSW, LMHC, or LMFT). LMHCs and LMFTs must hold New York’s diagnostic privilege. License must have no current restrictions or pending disciplinary action.

•
Master’s degree in Social Work, Mental Health Counseling, Marriage and Family Therapy, Clinical Mental Health Counseling, or another behavioral health discipline that meets New York licensure requirements; or a doctoral degree (Psy.D. or Ph.D.) in Clinical Psychology, Counseling Psychology, or a related psychology discipline.

•
Experience providing evidence-based behavioral health treatment to children, adolescents, young adults, and families.

•
Demonstrated ability to deliver culturally responsive, trauma-informed, and developmentally appropriate care that recognizes and respects members' identities, lived experiences, family structures, and backgrounds.

•
Experience utilizing evidence-based interventions such as CBT, DBT, ACT, MI, PMT, EMDR, and other clinically appropriate treatment approaches.

•
Experience engaging caregivers as collaborative partners in treatment while promoting developmentally appropriate member autonomy.

•
Experience working collaboratively within an interdisciplinary care team.

•
Strong clinical judgment with excellent communication, organization, and documentation skills.

•
Tech-savvy and comfortable utilizing telehealth platforms, electronic health records, and other digital tools to deliver high-quality virtual care.

•
Warm, engaging, and collaborative clinical style with the ability to build therapeutic rapport across developmental stages.

This remote position reports to the Supervisor, Neurodiversity Navigation.

As a Neurodiversity Navigator, you’ll be doing the important and meaningful work of supporting individuals as they navigate through the complex landscape of care for neurodiversity. You will provide critical psychoeducation on topics like early intervention services, behavioral strategies to address neurodiversity-related needs, navigating a diagnosis, and how to advocate for school, government and workplace accommodation services. Additionally, you will help connect clients to high-quality, evidence-based diagnosticians, services, and providers, depending on their needs. The focus of this role includes (but is not limited to) providing support to caregivers of children/adolescents with suspected or diagnosed neurodiverse conditions, supporting adults seeking neuroaffirming and neurodiversity-informed care, and assisting clients with navigating assessment services and support resources. This position does not involve in-person services or therapy, but rather provides support to individuals and families related to neurodiversity via phone, video conference, and/or email.

Responsibilities
• Support clients by understanding their current situation, conducting a brief assessment related to needs and potential risk concerns, providing psychoeducation relevant to the client and their needs, creating a client-centered care plan, and connecting the client to treatment or support options and resources.

•
Use an assessment rubric to determine whether neuropsychological testing is indicated for a given Lyra member, based on history, presenting concerns, and other factors. If testing is recommended, you will also help to assess whether a member is appropriate for virtual or in-person neuropsychological testing.

•
Administer psychoeducational training to caregivers of children/teens with neurodiverse conditions in order to help them learn skills to address behavior and neurodiversity-related needs, as well as to improve caregiving strategies.

•
Serve as a neurodiversity subject matter expert—providing guidance on how to best handle situations involving neurodiverse needs, consulting with cross-functional and clinical teams regarding best practices in the context of neurodiversity, and contributing to establishing strong provider partnerships.

•
Independently manage a caseload of complex, multi-need, neurodiverse clients , providing collaborative case management.

•
Successfully facilitate ongoing engagement, supporting clients as they move through various levels of care, employing neuroaffirming strategies to support client readiness for treatment.

•
Manage client crises, providing brief risk and needs assessments, and connecting the client to treatment or crisis resources when needed.

•
Respond to in-the-moment callers seeking crisis support, offering brief, evidence-based coping skills.

•
Effectively and professionally communicate with clients and providers throughout the process of accessing care, via modalities such as email, phone, care portal/EHR, and videoconferencing.

•
Creatively troubleshoot roadblocks to offering personalized, high quality clinical care options for our clients.

•
Use Lyra’s proprietary matching software, as well as other methods including facility database, health plan directory, and internet searches to identify treatment options for clients, and connect clients to the evidence-based treatment options, based on each individual client’s specific needs and preferences.

•
During caregiver training, administer and monitor measures to assess overall caregiver strain and stress.

•
Participate in and present cases for discussion in multidisciplinary clinical consultation team meetings, when needed.

•
Coordinate care and communicate with clients’ health plans, billing team, and/or clinical and support teams.

• Provide feedback to leadership for continuous program improvement, including suggestions to improve client experience, operational efficiencies, or outcomes.

Master’s degree Board Certified Behavior Analyst; BCBA certification and/or independent licensure is required. We’re unable to provide supervised hours toward licensure.

•
Significant experience managing neurodiversity-related clinical situations (preference towards experience providing case management expertise)

•
Experience providing training and/or education regarding behavior and neurodiversity-related topics to caregivers and/or clients

•
Deep understanding of the neurodiversity care navigation landscape at the national, state, and regional levels, for both children and adults

•
Comfort in environments with constantly evolving responsibilities

•
Passion for connecting individuals with excellent client-centered care and ability to provide short-term support via phone, videoconferencing, and email

•
Bilingual, Spanish-speaking candidates strongly preferred, but not required

Pacific time zone (e.g., such as 9am-5pm PT, 10am-6pm PT) preferred, but not required

About the Role
The Lyra Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) program provides comprehensive DBT for adults and adolescents. Both the adult and adolescent programs involve weekly individual therapy, weekly DBT skills training groups, and weekly consultation team meetings for DBT therapists. All Lyra DBT clients also have 24/7 access to a team of licensed clinicians who have been trained in DBT skills coaching for around the clock support.
As a Lyra DBT Therapist, you’ll provide individual DBT, multifamily skills groups, and parenting and family sessions for adolescents and their parents, as well as individual DBT and DBT skills groups as needed for adult clients. You’ll also assign DBT-relevant digital lessons, videos, and assessments to your clients to enhance learnings and monitor outcomes between sessions. Lyra's clients come from a multitude of backgrounds and experiences, and have varying needs and abilities. We strive to continue to meet their unique needs by delivering culturally responsive care—an approach that accounts for the impact of cultural backgrounds on each person’s care experience.
Our therapists enjoy connecting with their colleagues who share a passion for providing evidence-based care. You’ll attend weekly consultation team meetings as well as one-on-one consultation meetings with an expert DBT team lead, co-lead DBT skills groups with other DBT providers, and attend robust trainings to enhance your clinical skills. You always have a team behind you if a crisis comes up. You’re never alone, even while working remotely in the US.
This role may be a great fit if you are a New York licensed clinician with experience providing comprehensive DBT to adolescents and adults. You may also find this role rewarding if:
You are passionate about helping others improve their lives through skills-based interventions and work to understand your clients through a lens of compassion and curiosity.
You enjoy evidence-based practice, continual learning, and professional improvement.
You prefer to work within a collaborative team environment.
You are accountable for your own outcomes and performance, and are willing to embrace challenges that others may shy away from.
You’re interested in a flexible part-time role.

• Unrestricted, active New York license (able to work independently without supervision from a licensed supervisor) without current or pending disciplinary action

• Any New York LMFT/LCSW licenses must have diagnostic privilege

•
Formal didactic training in DBT required (e.g., in-house training with consultation team, tape review, 1:1 supervision; Behavioral Tech; DBT Foundational Training; DBT Intensive Training)

•
One year minimum experience providing comprehensive DBT to adolescents which includes: individual DBT therapy with clients through Stage 1 of treatment, facilitating skills groups utilizing Linehan materials, participation on a consultation team, skills coaching

•
DBT-LBC certification preferred but not required

•
Experience, comfort, and passion working with clients who present with high risk behaviors, including suicidal ideation and/or self-injury

•
Willingness to obtain cross-licensing in additional states as needed to support program growth

•
Experience providing telehealth therapy services in a virtual environment (video and teletherapy) preferred but not required

•
Computer and live video tools literacy (e.g., Zoom, Google Meets, DoxyMe, Skype, etc.)

We are looking for contract psychiatrists who are passionate about whole-person, whole family mental health care and working within a connected network to provide patients with easily accessible, culturally responsive, high-quality mental health care.

About the Role
The Lyra Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) program provides comprehensive DBT for adults and adolescents. Both the adult and adolescent programs involve weekly individual therapy, weekly DBT skills training groups, and weekly consultation team meetings for DBT therapists. All Lyra DBT clients also have 24/7 access to a team of licensed clinicians who have been trained in DBT skills coaching for around the clock support.
As a Lyra DBT Therapist, you’ll provide individual DBT, multifamily skills groups, and parenting and family sessions for adolescents and their parents, as well as individual DBT and DBT skills groups as needed for adult clients. You’ll also assign DBT-relevant digital lessons, videos, and assessments to your clients to enhance learnings and monitor outcomes between sessions. Lyra's clients come from a multitude of backgrounds and experiences, and have varying needs and abilities. We strive to continue to meet their unique needs by delivering culturally responsive care—an approach that accounts for the impact of cultural backgrounds on each person’s care experience.
Our therapists enjoy connecting with their colleagues who share a passion for providing evidence-based care. You’ll attend weekly consultation team meetings as well as one-on-one consultation meetings with an expert DBT team lead, co-lead DBT skills groups with other DBT providers, and attend robust trainings to enhance your clinical skills. You always have a team behind you if a crisis comes up. You’re never alone, even while working remotely in the US.
This role may be a great fit if you are a Massachusetts licensed clinician with experience providing comprehensive DBT to adolescents and adults. You may also find this role rewarding if:
You are passionate about helping others improve their lives through skills-based interventions and work to understand your clients through a lens of compassion and curiosity.
You enjoy evidence-based practice, continual learning, and professional improvement.
You prefer to work within a collaborative team environment.
You are accountable for your own outcomes and performance, and are willing to embrace challenges that others may shy away from.
You’re interested in a flexible part-time role.

Requirements
•
Unrestricted, active Massachusetts license (able to work independently without supervision from a licensed supervisor) without current or pending disciplinary action

•
Formal didactic training in DBT required (e.g., in-house training with consultation team, tape review, 1:1 supervision; Behavioral Tech; DBT Foundational Training; DBT Intensive Training)

•
One year minimum experience providing comprehensive DBT to adolescents which includes: individual DBT therapy with clients through Stage 1 of treatment, facilitating skills groups utilizing Linehan materials, participation on a consultation team, skills coaching

•
DBT-LBC certification preferred but not required

•
Experience, comfort, and passion working with clients who present with high risk behaviors, including suicidal ideation and/or self-injury

•
Willingness to obtain cross-licensing in additional states as needed to support program growth

•
Experience providing telehealth therapy services in a virtual environment (video and teletherapy) preferred but not required

•
Computer and live video tools literacy (e.g., Zoom, Google Meets, DoxyMe, Skype, etc.)

About Us:

Rent the Runway (RTR) is transforming the way we get dressed by pioneering the world’s first Closet in the Cloud. Founded in 2009, RTR has disrupted the $2.4 trillion fashion industry by inspiring women with a more joyful, sustainable and financially-savvy way to feel their best every day. As the ultimate destination for circular fashion, the brand now offers infinite points of access to its shared closet via a fully customizable subscription to fashion, one-time rental, or ownership. RTR offers designer apparel and accessories from hundreds of brand partners and has built in-house proprietary technology and a one-of-a-kind reverse logistics operation. RTR has been named to CNBC’s “Disruptor 50” five times in ten years, and has been placed on Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies list multiple times.

About the Job:

As the General Manager (GM) of Subscription, you will lead and accelerate the growth of RTR’s core membership business, the subscription that gives customers ongoing access to our shared closet. Members choose their plan, rotate styles through the month, and can pause or change their plan as their lives change. This role gives you a meaningful opportunity to serve millions of women over time and shape the experience that keeps them coming back.

As a GM, you will have P&L responsibility over this core revenue stream for RTR and will be responsible for setting the vision, driving an aggressive growth strategy, and executing against a comprehensive roadmap to unlock the next phase of growth for Subscription.

You will operate at the intersection of acquisition, retention, product, merchandising, pricing, inventory, and operations, leading a cross-functional team to deliver a best-in-class member experience and strong financial performance. This is an ideal role for a strategic, data-driven operator who can move seamlessly between vision and execution, and is excited to scale a consumer-facing membership business.

This is a full-time role reporting to one of RTR’s Executive team members overseeing Commercial Revenue and will be part of the company’s extended leadership team.

Responsibilities:

• Own the Subscription Business (GM + P&L Ownership): Own the P&L for the Subscription business, including revenue growth, contribution margin, and cost structure. Define and execute a strategy to scale membership, including new growth levers, member segments, and plan options. Establish clear KPIs and performance dashboards to measure success.

• Drive Member Acquisition & Growth: In partnership with Marketing, drive new member acquisition across paid, organic, affiliate, and partner channels, with a focus on efficient customer acquisition cost and payback. Build the measurement and attribution approach that tells us where growth is coming from and where to invest.

• Lead Retention, Pausing & Lifecycle: Reduce churn and improve member lifetime value through lifecycle marketing, personalized recommendations, loyalty program optimization, and proactive engagement. Design and test offers and plan changes that keep members active without eroding margin.

• Optimize Pricing, Promotions & Add-On Revenue: Set the framework for membership pricing, promotional depth, and add-on revenue, balancing acquisition, retention, and margin. Maximize traffic, conversion, and revenue per member.

• Guide Product & Technology Roadmap: Define and prioritize the subscription product roadmap in partnership with Product and Engineering. Build and ship features that create a seamless, frictionless, and delightful end-to-end shopping experience, including UX from discovery and onboarding through personalization, conversion, and self-serve member management.

• Optimize Assortment & Inventory for Members: Partner with Buying, Site Merchandising, and Inventory teams to curate assortment that keeps members engaged and drives improvements in inventory utilization, availability, and new-unit efficiency.

• Improve Operations & Fulfillment: Partner with Operations to ensure a reliable shipping, returns, and reverse logistics experience that supports the monthly membership rhythm.

• Cross-Functional Leadership: Lead a cross-functional team spanning product, engineering, merchandising, marketing, and operations while serving as the central point of accountability for Subscription performance. Present regular business updates, insights, and strategic recommendations to executive leadership.

• Test, Learn, & Reimagine: Build a culture of rapid experimentation and iteration while identifying opportunities to reimagine the membership experience to drive step-change growth. Stay ahead of industry trends in e-commerce, fashion, and subscription business models.

About You:

• 10+ years of experience in strategy, operations, product, or general management roles within e-commerce, subscription, retail, or consumer-facing businesses.

• Proven experience owning a subscription, membership, or consumer business line or P&L, with a strong understanding of acquisition economics, retention drivers, and cost structures, and the ability to deliver quantifiable business impact.

• Strong track record of driving growth, executing cross-functional initiatives, and operating with a high level of autonomy in dynamic and fast-paced environments.

• Experience with lifecycle marketing, CRM, growth marketing, or subscription retention strategies.

• Experience working closely with Product and Engineering teams to build, test, and launch customer-facing features.

• Highly analytical and data-driven, with the ability to translate insights into action and measure incrementality.

• Comfortable operating at both strategic and executional levels, from setting vision to rolling up your sleeves with a “no task is too small” mindset.

• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with experience presenting to executive leadership and gaining alignment across multiple stakeholders with varying priorities.

• Passion for delivering exceptional customer experiences as well as for the broader fashion-tech and rental/resale economy.

• Experience in fashion/apparel, digital merchandising, membership programs, and/or optimizing conversion funnels is preferred.

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

This is a dynamic, high energy role in which you will bring the Internet of Things to mid-sized customers, building Samsara's business and bringing the benefits of sensor data to customers. Typical sales will be $20k to $100k, and involve POCs, multiple stakeholders, managing trials, multi-faceted pricing negotiations, and selling to executives and CXOs.

This role is open for candidates residing in the following US states: Maine, New Hampshire, Vermont, Massachusetts , Rhode Island, Connecticut, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Washinton DC, Maryland, Delaware. The role requires travel approximately 25% of the time.

You should apply if:

• You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

• Your mantra is #alwaysbeprospecting: The world of operations is vast. Your customers are often out in the field and the best way to catch them is live on the phone. Samsara’s top reps do constant research to find companies and contacts to expand their pipeline.

• You have innate curiosity in how businesses work: One day you’ll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.

• You are a life-long learner: Samsara sales are complex. You will need to learn about businesses where you previously had little knowledge. The payoff is big but you have to be willing to put in the work.

• You build genuine relationships with your customers: The industries we serve have relied on pen-and-paper solutions for years and haven’t been met with the type of technology we offer. Our customers value earned trust and human relationships built over time.

• You want to be with the best: Samsara’s high-performance Sales culture means you’ll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.

Minimum requirements for this role:

• 2+ years experience in a full-cycle, closing sales role

• Experience independently closing new deals larger than $10,000 in annual revenue

•

All candidates must be located in one of the following states: Maine, New Hampshire, Vermont, Massachusetts , Rhode Island, Connecticut, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Washinton DC, Maryland, Delaware

An ideal candidate has:

• Proven track record of consistent quota achievement

• Experience selling in the midmarket space - medium to large deals sizes

• Experience with high-volume cold calling

• Must demonstrate a growth mindset and a willingness to be collaborative with your teammates and in your selling process

• SFDC familiarity

The compensation range shown spans approved pay zones for this role. Your primary work location determines the range applicable to you, which may be narrower than the full range displayed.

Annual on-target earnings (OTE) range for full-time employees for this position is below and depends on your city of residence. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual OTE Salary

$152,000 — $190,000 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email accessibleinterviewing@samsara.com or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu , a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here .

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

This is a dynamic, high energy role in which you will bring the Internet of Things to mid-sized customers, building Samsara's business and bringing the benefits of sensor data to customers. Typical sales will be $20k to $100k, and involve POCs, multiple stakeholders, managing trials, multi-faceted pricing negotiations, and selling to executives and CXOs.

This role is open for candidates residing in the following US states: Texas, Oklahoma, Louisiana, Arkansas, Kansas, Missouri, Mississippi, Alabama. The role requires travel approximately 25% of the time.

You should apply if:

• You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

• Your mantra is #alwaysbeprospecting: The world of operations is vast. Your customers are often out in the field and the best way to catch them is live on the phone. Samsara’s top reps do constant research to find companies and contacts to expand their pipeline.

• You have innate curiosity in how businesses work: One day you’ll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.

• You are a life-long learner: Samsara sales are complex. You will need to learn about businesses where you previously had little knowledge. The payoff is big but you have to be willing to put in the work.

• You build genuine relationships with your customers: The industries we serve have relied on pen-and-paper solutions for years and haven’t been met with the type of technology we offer. Our customers value earned trust and human relationships built over time.

• You want to be with the best: Samsara’s high-performance Sales culture means you’ll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.

Minimum requirements for this role:

• 2+ years experience in a full-cycle, closing sales role

• Experience independently closing new deals larger than $10,000 in annual revenue

• All candidates must be located in one of the following US states: Texas, Oklahoma, Louisiana, Arkansas, Kansas, Missouri, Mississippi, Alabama.

An ideal candidate has:

• Proven track record of consistent quota achievement

• Experience selling in the midmarket space - medium to large deals sizes

• Experience with high-volume cold calling

• Must demonstrate a growth mindset and a willingness to be collaborative with your teammates and in your selling process

• SFDC familiarity

The compensation range shown spans approved pay zones for this role. Your primary work location determines the range applicable to you, which may be narrower than the full range displayed.

Annual on-target earnings (OTE) range for full-time employees for this position is below and depends on your city of residence. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual OTE Salary

$152,000 — $190,000 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email accessibleinterviewing@samsara.com or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu , a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here .

About the role:

Samsara is looking for an experienced manager to lead SOX business process compliance and help keep the trust in our financial reporting as strong as the business we’re building. As part of our SOX Compliance team, you’ll help oversee and strengthen Samsara’s global control environment, protecting the accuracy of our financial reporting and keeping us compliant as we scale. You’ll partner closely with IT and business process owners to design and implement controls, spot gaps early, and drive remediation to the finish line. We’re looking for someone who takes real ownership. You bring deep, hands-on SOX expertise, a track record of delivering projects reliably, and the confidence to run with complex work independently. If you take pride in being the person others count on to get it done right, we’d love to meet you.

This is a remote position open to candidates based in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.

You should apply if:

• You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

• You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.

• You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.

• You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-calibre team that will encourage you to do your best.

In this role, you will:

• Develop, lead, and execute periodic financial risk assessments, materiality calculations, and scoping of the SOX program

• Develop and deliver training to SOX control owners, including process documentation, testing methodology, management review controls, and controls over Information Produced by the Entity (IPE).

• Conduct walkthroughs across all business process areas and work with business process owners to ensure timely review and updates to the control documentation

• Collaborate cross functionally to design leading edge practices with a financial compliance mindset across several complex business process areas.

• Monitor and assess emerging financial reporting risks with the growth and evolution of the business and develop plans to implement appropriate controls to timely address these emerging risks

• Ownership of control deficiency evaluation, aggregation analysis as well as development and execution of related remediation plans.

• Help drive the SOX AI transformation strategy by identifying high-value opportunities, implementing AI-enabled solutions, and driving adoption and new ways of working across the global SOX organization.

• Provide reporting to business leaders on program status, health, and effectiveness of the business process control environment

• Collaborate and align with the company’s external audit and internal audit around financial reporting risks, design of ICFR monitoring systems,and SOX program approach

• Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

Minimum requirements for the role:

• 7+ years of SOX 404 / ICFR experience at a Big Four (internal or external audit) or combination of Big Four and public company experience

• Hands-on experience with risk assessment, scoping, walkthroughs, control design, and deficiency evaluation

• Strong knowledge of order to cash, procure to pay, financial close and reporting controls

• Ability to identify, assess and explain risks and control gaps clearly to executives and other non-technical audiences

• Working knowledge of COSO 2013, PCAOB AS 2201, and SEC ICFR guidance, including management review controls and IPE

• Bachelor's in accounting or finance (CPA and/or CIA preferred)

An ideal candidate also has:

• Experience with financial systems such as Netsuite, Salesforce, Workday and Xactly

• Experience using automation or AI tools to make compliance work faster, more reliable, and SOX compliant

• Experience working closely with Internal Audit and External Auditors

• Strong communication skills, including presenting to and influencing senior business leaders

• Demonstrated success managing worksteams/project independently

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Samsara's Customer Success team is on the front lines of business value delivery by helping customers adopt our platform, realize measurable business value, and renew and expand with confidence. Billing errors, concession requests, and cancellation or return exceptions currently land with CSMs, CS managers, and several partner teams, each holding part of the picture. As our customer base and billing complexity have grown, these cases take too long, repeat for the same reasons, and pull CSMs away from adoption and renewal work. As the Contract and Billing Resolution Specialist, you will be the single owner of complex billing and contract cases for Mid-Market and Commercial accounts.

You will take a customer's report that something is wrong with their bill, work out what happened across systems and teams, choose the right path to fix it, and see it through, keeping the customer informed. It is part detective, part project manager, part customer advocate. You will also tell the teams who own the underlying systems and processes what keeps breaking.

Your role will be cross-functional, working alongside and connecting Customer Success Managers, Sales, Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal. This is a new role, and you will help shape the case record, the root-cause tags, and the monthly read-out that define how Customer Success resolves billing and contract cases at Samsara.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.

You should apply if:

• You want to impact the industries that run our world: Every phone call you answer and every email you send can affect whether truck drivers deliver goods on time and without accidents, whether students get dropped off safely from school, or whether power gets restored quickly after a natural disaster.

• You thrive the most when solving problems: Our constantly expanding technology and the complexities faced by our customers provide an exciting range of challenges for our Customer Success teams. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you will strategically partner with our customers to find unique solutions to help keep their operations safe, efficient, and sustainable.

• You are a natural relationship builder: Whether the relationship is with our customers or with cross-functional teams in Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team.

• You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. This Customer Success team is still shaping its future and you will have plenty of autonomy and opportunities to master your craft in a hyper growth environment.

• You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals out there.

In this role, you will:

• Own complex billing and contract cases for Mid-Market and Commercial accounts, from the first report to a confirmed fix, and keep the customer informed in plain terms, including accounts that are delinquent or facing suspension.

• Reconstruct the full story behind a billing error across contracts, order forms, segment or ownership changes, reprocessing, and invoicing, including cases with several AE handoffs and no clean record of what was promised.

• Separate a correction of a Samsara error from a concession, a return, a reprocess, and a contract amendment, and choose the path that fixes the customer's billing, not only the immediate complaint.

• Drive Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal to execute the fix.

• Evaluate and prepare concession requests: confirm whether Samsara was at fault, size the request against policy and the approval matrix, write a short case summary (what happened, root cause, options considered and ruled out, recommendation, and risk), route it to the right approver, and confirm the credit is applied and the customer told.

• Support cancellation, return, and ETF exceptions: validate eligibility (purchase and renewal dates, trial history, Return ACV, financing partner, documentation), prepare the case for the approving team, act as the Customer Success fallback when the first approver does not respond within the window, and make sure approved outcomes are processed.

• Be the front door for billing, concession, and cancellation requests: log every request in a single case record, including those that arrive via Slack, email, or Gainsight; redirect them to the right path; and coach CSMs and AEs on what a complete request looks like.

• Fix repeat causes: tag the root cause on every case, separate one-offs from systemic failures, and deliver a monthly read-out to the teams that own the systems and processes involved.

• Carry forward the billing improvement work with Support, Finance, and Product, including earlier detection of billing problems that threaten renewals.

• Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's operating principles, including Keep a High Bar, Be Intellectually Honest, and Solve Problems Together, as we scale.

Minimum requirements for the role:

• 4+ years of experience in billing operations, order to cash, revenue operations, deal desk, contracts, or a similar finance and operations role.

• This is a demanding position with high internal visibility that requires strong priority management and high emotional intelligence.

• Strong investigative skills: you can rebuild a timeline from incomplete or conflicting information across CRM, billing, and contract systems, including when the people involved have left.

• Sound financial judgment about credits, concessions, reprocessing, and refunds, and a clear way of explaining your recommendation.

• Customer-facing communication that stays honest and composed in hard conversations, and written summaries a leader can read once and decide on.

• A record of driving results across teams without authority over them, including working to deadlines in an approval process.

• Familiarity with order forms, amendments, and terms, and how they flow into billing.

• Comfort with ambiguity and incomplete precedent, and rigorous case management so nothing drops across weeks and stakeholders.

• Diplomacy, tact, and poise under pressure when working through customer issues.

An ideal candidate also has:

• Experience handling escalated or high-dollar billing disputes.

• Experience with Salesforce, NetSuite, or an equivalent ERP, and CPQ tools. We also use Zendesk, Gainsight, and Sweethawk.

• Customer Success, Support, or account management background with customer-facing financial or contract work.

• Experience building or improving billing dispute processes.

• Exposure to subscription or hardware-plus-subscription billing.

• AI First: Experience using AI tooling to drive efficiency and outcomes.

• Strong bias for action and insistence on high standards

Samsara's Customer Success team is on the front lines of business value delivery by helping customers adopt our platform, realize measurable business value, and renew and expand with confidence. Today, billing errors, concession requests, and cancellation or return exceptions land with CSMs, CS managers, and several partner teams, each holding part of the picture. No one owns the whole timeline. We are creating a dedicated Contract and Billing Resolution team to close that gap for Mid-Market and Commercial accounts.

As the Manager, Contract and Billing, you will lead this new team of 3 to 4 Contract and Billing Resolution Specialists. You will inherit work that CSMs and their managers have handled as best they can, and turn it into a function that is repeatable, measurable, and scalable: the playbook, the intake and routing, the system of record, the root-cause reporting, and the hiring and coaching of the people who do the work.

This role sits between the sales process and the finance process. A bill can look wrong because of something that happened upstream in a quote, an order form, a contract, or a segment change in Salesforce, or downstream in billing and invoicing. You and your team will figure out where it broke, regardless of which team caused it, and work across both sides to fix it. You will partner closely with Customer Success Managers, Sales, Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal, and report the repeat failures to the teams that own the underlying systems and processes.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.

You should apply if:

• You want to impact the industries that run our world: Every billing case your team resolves keeps the organizations that move goods, transport students, and restore power focused on their operations rather than on a billing dispute.

• You want to build something from the ground up: This team and function are new. You will hire the team, write the playbook, and set up the systems and metrics that define how Samsara resolves billing and contract cases.

• You thrive when solving problems: You figure things out, even without a clean playbook or precedent. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you find the fix that works for the customer and for Samsara, and you teach your team to do the same.

• You are an investigator: You enjoy rebuilding a timeline from incomplete or conflicting records across sales and finance systems, and you stay curious until the numbers tie out.

• You are a people leader: You enjoy hiring, coaching, and developing a team, and you set a high bar for quality, ownership, and follow-through.

• You are a natural relationship builder: Whether with our customers or cross-functional teams at Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team, and you can maintain clear boundaries while staying warm.

• You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together, and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals.

• Build and lead a new team of 3 to 4 Contract and Billing Resolution Specialists: hire, onboard, coach, and develop them, and set clear expectations for case quality, ownership, and customer communication.

• Stand up the function from scratch: take the billing, concession, and cancellation work that CSMs handle today, define what the team owns and what it does not, and turn it into a documented playbook that is repeatable and scalable.

• Design and launch the system of record for billing and contract cases, working with CS Ops and Systems partners to set up intake, routing, case tracking, and customer communication in tools such as Zendesk, Salesforce, or Jira.

• Own the front door: make sure every billing, concession, and cancellation request is logged in one place, including those that arrive through Slack, email, or Gainsight, and coach CSMs and AEs on what a complete request looks like.

• Act as the escalation point for the most complex, sensitive, or high-dollar cases, including accounts that are delinquent or facing suspension, and step in directly with customers and internal leaders when needed.

• Define the handoffs, ownership, and service levels with Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal so cases stop bouncing between teams.

• Set the standards for how the team separates a correction of a Samsara error from a concession, a return, a reprocess, and a contract amendment, and how concession and cancellation exceptions are sized, documented, and routed through the approval matrix.

• Build the metrics and reporting for the function, including volume, days to resolution, repeat errors, concession dollars, and renewal risk tied to billing issues, and use them to manage the team and show impact.

• Fix repeat causes: own the root-cause tagging on every case, separate one-offs from systemic failures, and deliver a monthly read-out to the teams that own the systems and processes involved, such as segment-move bugs, term rounding, and AE handoff gaps.

• Partner with Support, Finance, Sales Ops, and Product on billing improvement work, including earlier detection of billing problems that threaten renewals.

• Use AI to improve how the team works, from structuring case timelines to drafting summaries, while keeping approvals, amounts, and root-cause conclusions with people.

• Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's operating principles, including Keep a High Bar, Be Intellectually Honest, and Solve Problems Together, as we scale.

• 2+ years of experience managing people, ideally in a sales operations or finance capacity.

• Experience building a team or function from scratch, or leading a major reorganization of an existing team, including writing the playbook and processes that made the work repeatable.

• Deep working knowledge of either the quote-to-contract side (quotes, order forms, amendments, terms, and the sales systems that pass contract data downstream) or the billing side (invoicing, credits, rebills, and collections), and the curiosity to learn the other.

• Experience setting up or significantly improving a case management, ticketing, or request-routing system, such as Zendesk, Jira, or Salesforce cases, that worked for both customers and internal teams.

• Strong investigative skills: you can rebuild a timeline from incomplete or conflicting information across CRM, billing, and contract systems, and teach others to do the same.

• Sound financial judgment about credits, concessions, reprocessing, and refunds, and a clear way of explaining your recommendation.

• A record of driving results across teams without authority over them, including Sales, Finance, and Operations partners with competing priorities.

• Customer-facing communication that stays honest and composed in hard conversations, and written summaries a leader can read once and decide on.

• This is a demanding position with high internal visibility that requires strong priority management, high emotional intelligence, and comfort with ambiguity and incomplete precedent.

An ideal candidate also has:

• Has worked on both sides: the sales process and contracting, and the finance and billing process.

• Has managed a team that handled escalated or high-dollar billing or contract disputes.

• Has experience with Salesforce, NetSuite, and CPQ tools. Familiarity with Zendesk, Gainsight, and Sweethawk.

• Has a Customer Success, Support, or account management background with customer-facing financial or contract work.

• Has built dashboards, service levels, or root-cause reporting that changed how other teams fixed their processes.

• Has exposure to subscription or hardware-plus-subscription billing.

• AI First: Experience using AI tooling to drive efficiency and outcomes for themselves and their team.

• Has a strong bias for action and insistence on high standards.

• You use AI tools daily and get excited when a new model changes what's possible.

• You have strong commercial instincts and want to understand how the product gets sold.

• You have conviction and can move a room quickly, but low ego in changing your mind when someone else is right (or more right).

If that sounds like you, let's go.

• Support experienced responders during major security incidents through evidence collection, technical analysis, and agreed containment and recovery actions.

• Maintain clear investigation records and provide useful updates and handovers to teammates across regions.

• Improve runbooks, help tune detections, and contribute small scripts or automated workflows with guidance and review from teammates.

• Participate in post-incident reviews and turn lessons learned into practical improvements.

• Champion Samsara’s cultural principles: Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, and Win as a Team.

• Hands-on experience triaging and investigating security alerts in a security operations, incident response or similar role.

• Experience using security tools such as a SIEM, endpoint detection and response platform, or email security platform to investigate suspicious activity.

• An understanding of common threats, such as phishing, account compromise and suspicious endpoint activity, and the networking, operating system and identity concepts needed to investigate them.

• Ability to query and interpret logs, distinguish evidence from assumptions, and recognise when further investigation or escalation is needed.

• Some scripting experience: you can read, adapt and write small scripts in Python or another language to support an investigation or simplify repetitive work.

• Clear written and verbal communication, including documenting findings, explaining uncertainty and providing effective handovers.

• A careful approach to sensitive information, willingness to ask for help, and openness to feedback.

• Experience investigating activity in cloud platforms such as AWS or GCP, SaaS applications, or identity systems.

• Exposure to writing or tuning detections, threat hunting, or investigating activity across multiple data sources.

• Experience using Python, APIs or automation platforms to improve a security workflow.

• Familiarity with evidence collection or forensic analysis on macOS, Windows or Linux.

You do not need experience in every area above. Bring a solid operational foundation, curiosity and a willingness to learn.

• Experience with new product introductions, product transitions and end-of-life planning.

• Experience using AI-assisted tools to improve planning workflows.

• Familiarity with MEDDPICC and/or Command of the Message sales frameworks

• Own the layers everything else depends on. Peripheral drivers, secure bootloaders, device firmware updates, as well as the core management layers like power and connectivity, that determine whether a device in the field quietly recovers on its own or becomes an RMA.

• Chase every microamp. Design protocols and hardware management for battery-powered sensors and gateways where the gap between good firmware and great firmware is measured in years of device life.

• You have led firmware development for several new products end to end. You have taken firmware from initial concept through architecture, technical implementation, validation, and product launch, providing hands-on technical leadership throughout.

• Substantial bare-metal and RTOS experience - Zephyr, FreeRTOS, or equivalent. You have made scheduling, memory and timing decisions. Mutexes and semaphores are everyday tools for you.

• You have brought up new boards. First power-on of unproven hardware, at the bench with the electrical engineer who drew it up, working out whether the bug is in your code, a library, the schematic, or the part itself.

• Fluency in the low-level interfaces - SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, ADC and the ability to debug the seam between hardware and software.

• Real bench instincts. The usage of an oscilloscope, network analyzer, or RF spectrum analyzer, is how you form a hypothesis, not what you reach for after the print statements run out.

• Senior-level scope. You have led work spanning hardware, firmware, cloud and quality from concept to shipped product. You have consistently driven consensus across teams.

• Cross-layer judgment. You can trace how a decision at the driver level surfaces in a customer's experience three layers up, and you make that trade-off on purpose.

• Fluency in C. You know what the compiler is doing, and you can read a linker map, a stack trace, or a corrupted heap without guessing.

• You write things down. Design docs, review comments and post-mortems that other engineers can actually act on.

• You ship fast without shipping badly. Comfortable iterating on customer feedback at speed, backed by automated testing and code you would be content to inherit.

• You use AI smartly. It’s part of your every day work flow and multiplies your output without watering things down.

• BLE at depth - You understand what’s going on down the PHY and can build orchestration for the system to use in a performant and power efficient way.

• Cellular IoT - LTE-M or NB-IoT modem integration, power state management, and the certification gauntlet (FCC, PTCRB, carrier approval).

• Securing embedded systems end to end - secure boot, firmware signing, cryptography, and key management that survives contact with manufacturing.

• OTA and device firmware update at fleet scale - A/B partitions, rollback, and the discipline of never bricking a device you cannot physically reach.

• You’ve been on the factory floor - You have an understanding of the processes behind the mass production and quality assurance of electronics. You have a track record of fixing production show stoppers.

Through a unique integration of sensor data such as GPS, acceleration, temperature, video, and more, we enable our customers to gain greater insights into operations, identify and eliminate inefficiencies, and react to alerts all in near real-time.

As a Firmware Engineer at Samsara, you will develop software that runs on millions of devices, deployed by our industrial and enterprise customers. You’ll tackle challenges including evaluating and selecting hardware components, bringing up new hardware platforms and sensors, building systems to gather data and detect meaningful events, and structuring recorded data to allow efficient analysis across thousands of devices while providing deep insights into individual events.

We use C for our MCU-based platforms, Golang for embedded applications on Linux-based gateways and backend services, Google protocol buffers to structure data, and various AWS technologies to process and store data. Experience with these exact technologies is not required.

What you bring

• 2+ years building firmware for resource-constrained systems , on products that shipped to real customers and then had to survive in the field.

• Fluency in C. You know what the compiler is doing, and you can read a linker map, a stack trace, or a corrupted heap without guessing.

• Solid bare-metal and RTOS experience - Zephyr, FreeRTOS, or equivalent. You have made scheduling, memory and timing decisions. Mutexes and semaphores are everyday tools for you.

• You have helped bring up new boards. First power-on of unproven hardware, at the bench with the electrical engineer who drew it up, working out whether the bug is in your code, a library, the schematic, or the part itself.

• Fluency in the low-level interfaces - SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, ADC and the ability to debug the seam between hardware and software.

• Real bench instincts. The usage of an oscilloscope, network analyzer, or RF spectrum analyzer, is how you form a hypothesis, not what you reach for after the print statements run out.

• Cross-team scope. You have contributed to work spanning hardware, firmware, cloud and quality from concept to shipped product. You have worked effectively across teams to build consensus.

• Cross-layer judgment. You can trace how a decision at the driver level surfaces in a customer's experience three layers up, and you factor that into your design decisions.

• You write things down. Design docs, review comments and post-mortems that other engineers can actually act on.

• You ship fast without shipping poorly. Comfortable iterating on customer feedback at speed, backed by automated testing and code you would be content to inherit.

• You use AI smartly. It’s part of your every day work flow and multiplies your output without watering things down.

• Cellular IoT - LTE-M or NB-IoT modem integration, power state management, and the certification gauntlet (FCC, PTCRB, carrier approval).

About Schoolhouse

Founded by Sal Khan, Schoolhouse is a peer-to-peer learning platform that delivers human connection and develops durable skills through online learning to best prepare students to thrive in the age of AI. So far, we’ve reached 200k+ learners from 180+ countries and we plan to grow to millions.

About the Vision

Our vision is to provide an education safety net to ensure that no talent goes undiscovered and that every student feels empowered in our changing world. We do this by bringing high school students together around learning to create an environment where they can develop and showcase academic mastery and durable skills.

At Schoolhouse, learning is academic, civic, and global. Students join tutoring sessions where peers help them reach academic goals through personalized support. They participate in Dialogues to discuss challenging issues and empathize across divides. Above all, students belong to a global community centered around human connection.

We believe this vision is ambitious, so we need a team that can move quickly in the face of ambiguity. We value sincerity and empathy and believe deeply in the power of human connection. We step in to help each other out, we think big but start small, we uplift each other, and we’re all learners at heart.

Learn more about our vision and our values here:

• Teen Helps 52-Year-Old Man Earn His High School Diploma

• The Power of Peer Tutoring

• Schoolhouse’s Public Roadmap

• What are Schoolhouse's community values?

About the Role

We’re looking for Senior Software Engineers who want to build stuff that’ll have an impact. You’ll join our 5-person engineering team and own full-stack features that hundreds of thousands of learners and tutors use worldwide.

Engineers at Schoolhouse have lots of ownership — you’ll work directly with our designer and other stakeholders to build out new experiments and streamline existing operations. We think the best way for engineers to build a quality product is to be involved early, drive progress, and stay close to our end users.

Scaling free quality interactions between students around the world comes with challenges that live at the intersection of UX, people ops, and technology. We need to both meet learner / tutor needs while ensuring that these interactions stay high quality and safe.

Some examples of what we’ve worked on include:

• Building an AI simulation & coach to help tutors practice for their first tutoring session

• Experimenting with new ways to connect tutors to learners wanting immediate homework help

• Creating a moderation system to automatically recognize and act on safety issues so humans can focus their time on the most important issues

Responsibilities

• Work with users and teammates to define problems, contribute product ideas, and lead work from prototypes / experiments through deployment.

• Break ambiguous work into manageable steps, coordinating contributions when needed

• Write simple, readable code and create / improve patterns that make future work easier.

• Help teammates grow through code reviews and pairing sessions

About You

If this sounds like you, we’d love for you to apply!

• [Senior] You’ve been a full-stack software engineer 3+ years and have a track record of leading full-stack projects from ambiguous problem through launch and iteration.

• [Senior] You can anticipate risks and make decisions that balance tradeoffs between speed, quality, and user experience.

• You have experience with Typescript, Node.js, React, Next.js, and Postgres (or can ramp up quickly).

• You build for users & have a nose for understanding what would help them the most.

• You move quickly while maintaining code quality. Perfect is the enemy of good.

• You fill in the gaps — you ask for help, but still work independently to figure things out. If necessary you can put on another hat if it’ll help users the most.

• You’re available to work in a US timezone.

Bonus points

• You have deep technical experience with our stack Typescript, Node.js, React, Next.js, Postgres, AWS, and GCP.

• You have experience building mobile apps.

• You have experience working in education or on an ed-tech product.

Life at Schoolhouse

• Work with an amazing team. We’ve got folks with backgrounds in education, consulting, astrophysics, startups, and more.

• Fully remote with flexible working hours. Meetings are in US Pacific Time mornings.

• Take real time off. We have unlimited PTO & use it. Folks regularly take time off throughout the year.

• Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits. Work-from-home stipend. Professional development budget. Health, dental, vision (for US employees).

• Semesterly retreats and monthly regional meetups

• Make an impact you can see. Check out our community stories page . Watch students help each other learn. See tutors grow into leaders. Your code will help real people learn and grow.

About the Application Process

• We might make some adjustments, but our expected interview process:

• A 30-minute intro screen to learn more about you and understand whether this role is a mutual fit

• A 45-minute screen where you'll read some code and brainstorm / prioritize product ideas

• A 1-hour programming interview where you’ll fix bugs and implement features on a toy repo

• A 1-hour systems design problem where you'll design a data model / api and handle challenges at scale

• A 45-minute culture fit call with non-technical team members

• Reference calls

We’re building an inclusive and equitable platform for learners across the world, and it’s important our core team reflects these principles too. Research shows people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we strongly encourage to you apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.

We’re here to give power to the patient.

For nearly 20 years, we’ve built the leading healthcare marketplace - helping tens of millions of people find and book the care they need. Now, we’re going further: building our infrastructure beyond Zocdoc’s marketplace to power access to care wherever patients search, from provider websites and insurance directories to search engines, AI platforms, and more.

Healthcare still lacks something every other major consumer industry takes for granted: a seamless way to go from seeking to getting . We don’t want to own the front door to care; there isn't one. We want to make sure all of those doors open when patients are knocking.

Fixing healthcare starts with fixing access to it. And we're still just getting started.

Your impact on our mission

Customer Success Managers help existing Zocdoc providers get more value from the platform and grow their practices. Through strategic outreach, they communicate the value of meeting with a CSM, and when running those meetings, they learn each practice’s goals, address operational challenges, and recommend ways to expand the partnership. This can include adding new providers to the platform, improving setup, or increasing the practice’s visibility. As product experts and trusted partners, CSMs help practices drive patient bookings, improve performance, and adopt features that support their growth.

You’ll enjoy this role if you are…

• Passionate about provider success and enjoy understanding practices’ goals and challenges to help drive feature adoption, utilization, and retention

• Comfortable balancing sales conversations, account management, and collaboration with internal teams

• Data-driven and consultative in your decision-making

• Motivated by a fast-paced, structured environment where you own your activity and results

Your day-to-day is...

• Drive practice performance by communicating feature value, addressing objections, helping practices maintain effective setup, and building provider buy-in

That means building an acquisition system that is relevant to the provider, responsive to intent, and accountable to real business outcomes.

You will define how we find the providers we are best positioned to serve, how we earn their attention, how we turn interest into action, and how we learn what creates durable growth. You will also own the performance of that system: balancing ROAS and efficiency with incremental new active providers, MQL quality, and the long-term value of the providers we acquire.

You will report to the VP, Provider Growth and help define what acquisition-led growth can look like at Zocdoc.

Your day-to-day...

• Build the strategy, roadmap, and operating model for Provider Acquisition, translating them into shipped programs and measurable business outcomes.

• Own acquisition performance and investment decisions: deliver MQL volume and quality, improve conversion to active providers, grow incremental new active providers, and meet ROAS or payback expectations while building long-term provider value.

• Establish the performance framework, data, instrumentation, attribution, and reporting that connect investment to MQLs, sign-ups, conversion, incremental lift, provider LTV, and revenue by segment, specialty, geography, account, and program. Use channel reporting and incrementality testing to distinguish true impact from credited activity.

• Define the audiences and markets where Zocdoc is best positioned to win, prioritize provider segments and account tiers, and match investment to opportunity, from scalable reach to 1:1, 1:few, and 1:many ABM.

• Reimagine acquisition as a connected growth system, bringing ABM, paid and organic search, web experiences, CRO, and field events together around shared audiences, messaging, and provider needs.

• Run a fast learning loop through bold experiments across audiences, channels, creative, offers, landing pages, journeys, events, partnerships, and emerging tools; scale what works and stop what does not.

• Partner with Sales, Product Marketing, Events, Marketing Operations, Data Science, and other growth leaders to align on audience definitions, handoffs, priorities, and decisions.

• Recruit, lead, coach, and develop the team; hire for the capabilities the function needs next, set a high bar, and create clarity across a growing portfolio of work.

• Lead the team’s priorities, planning, and operating cadence while staying close to the work, shaping strategy, reviewing creative and experiences, interrogating performance, and resolving obstacles as the function takes shape.

You’ll Enjoy This Role If You...

• Want a real builder challenge. We’ve experimented across ABM, paid and organic search, web, CRO, and events, but haven’t yet turned them into a connected, repeatable acquisition engine. You’ll help decide what to build, where to focus, and what to stop.

• Are motivated by ownership with visible business stakes. Your decisions will affect MQL quality, incremental active providers, ROAS or payback, conversion, and provider LTV.

• Are comfortable starting without a playbook. You can work with incomplete data and uneven foundations, form a point of view, get a test into market, learn quickly, and adjust.

• Like working at both altitudes: setting strategy and then getting into the details of audiences, campaigns, creative, landing pages, and performance data to unblock progress.

• Are excited to build the team as well as the function. There are teammates to partner with, but you’ll need to identify capability gaps, hire thoughtfully, and create clarity and momentum as the team grows.

• See paid, organic, web, ABM, and events as different ways to solve the same problem: helping the right providers discover, understand, and act on value.

• Are curious about new ways to find providers and earn their attention, including new channels, partnerships, content formats, data sources, and AI-enabled approaches and willing to test ideas that may not work before discovering the ones that do.

• Are energized by creating structure where today there is mostly ad hoc work and turning early lessons into repeatable capabilities.

You’ll Be Successful in This Role If You...

• Bring 10+ years leading acquisition, growth, demand generation, digital, performance, or integrated marketing, including 5+ years hiring and managing teams.

• Have built acquisition capabilities from strategy through activation, conversion, measurement, and scale.

• Bring deep expertise in performance marketing and strong working fluency across ABM, paid and organic search, SEO/AEO, website strategy, CRO, and field marketing.

• Have owned budgets and outcomes against a rigorous scorecard including ROAS or payback, incremental acquisition, MQL quality, funnel conversion, and provider or customer LTV.

• Connect channel performance to qualified pipeline, active providers, revenue, and durable provider value and make clear trade-offs between near-term efficiency and long-term growth.
